at hacke.explanation: "At hacke" means "to hack", to break into a computer, an account or a network without permission. Do not mix it up with at hakke (to chop), which has kk and is used for cutting or digging.

sentence.da: Nogen forsøgte at **hacke** firmaets netværk i går nat.
sentence.en: Someone tried to hack the company's network last night.

at hade.explanation: "At hade" means "to hate", and it is a strong word. For everyday dislikes, Danes often say something milder, like Jeg kan ikke lide (I don't like).

sentence.da: Man skal ikke **hade** andre.
sentence.en: You should not hate others.

at hagle.explanation: "At hagle" means "to hail", for ice falling from the sky as small hard balls. It is a weather verb that always starts with det, just like the weather verbs for rain and snow.

sentence.da: Det begynder at **hagle** med store, hårde isklumper.
sentence.en: It starts to hail with big, hard lumps of ice.

at hakke.explanation: "At hakke" means "to chop" or "to mince", cutting something into small pieces: Jeg hakker løg (I chop onions). Ground meat is hakket kød (chopped meat).

sentence.da: Man kan **hakke** persille med en skarp kniv.
sentence.en: You can chop parsley with a sharp knife.

at halte.explanation: "At halte" means "to limp", to walk unevenly because a leg or foot hurts. In speech it also describes something that works badly: Argumentet halter (The argument is weak).

sentence.da: Han vil **halte** i flere uger, fordi hans fod er brækket.
sentence.en: He will limp for several weeks because his foot is broken.

at halvere.explanation: "At halvere" means "to halve", to cut an amount to half of what it was, or to split something into two equal parts: En opskrift kan halveres (A recipe can be halved).

sentence.da: Butikken vil **halvere** prisen på alle varer.
sentence.en: The store will halve the price of all goods.

at handle.explanation: "At handle" means "to shop", and also "to act". Jeg handler i supermarkedet means "I shop at the supermarket", and at handle ind (to do the grocery shopping) is for food. With om (about) it means to be about something: Filmen handler om kærlighed (The film is about love).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **handle** i den nye butik.
sentence.en: I want to shop in the new store.

at handle ind.explanation: "At handle ind" means "to go grocery shopping": Jeg handler ind efter arbejde (I go grocery shopping after work). It is for food and everyday items. For clothes, say at shoppe (to shop).

sentence.da: Vi skal **handle ind**, fordi der ikke er mælk.
sentence.en: We have to go grocery shopping because there is no milk.

at handle om.explanation: "At handle om" means "to be about", for the topic of a book, film or talk: Filmen handler om en pige (The film is about a girl). Do not mix it up with at handle (to shop): Jeg handler i supermarkedet (I shop at the supermarket).

sentence.da: Min bog skal **handle om** en hund.
sentence.en: My book is going to be about a dog.

at harmonere.explanation: "At harmonere" means "to harmonize": to fit well together so that nothing feels out of place, for example colors, sounds or ideas. Add med to say with what: Gardinerne harmonerer med væggene (The curtains go well with the walls).

sentence.da: Gule og blå farver kan **harmonere** godt.
sentence.en: Yellow and blue colors can harmonize well.

at have.explanation: "At have" means "to have" or "to own". It is also used to say what you have done: Jeg har spist (I have eaten). Danish says Jeg har fødselsdag (literally I have birthday) where English says It is my birthday.

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **have** en kop kaffe.
sentence.en: I would like to have a cup of coffee.

at have ansvar for.explanation: "At have ansvar for" means "to be responsible for": Hun har ansvar for børnene (She is responsible for the children). Ansvar means "responsibility", so it is literally "to have responsibility for".

sentence.da: Læreren skal **have ansvar for** klassen.
sentence.en: The teacher has to be responsible for the class.

at have brug for.explanation: "At have brug for" means "to need": Jeg har brug for hjælp (I need help). Literally, it is to have use for. At behøve (to need) is also common, especially in du behøver ikke (you do not need to).

sentence.da: Man kan **have brug for** en paraply.
sentence.en: You may need an umbrella.

at have det sjovt.explanation: "At have det sjovt" means "to have fun": Børnene har det sjovt (The children are having fun). Have det (to feel) is also used for feelings in general: Jeg har det godt (I feel good).

sentence.da: Vi vil **have det sjovt** i weekenden.
sentence.en: We want to have fun this weekend.

at have en finger med i spillet.explanation: "At have en finger med i spillet" means "to be involved in something": to be one of the people responsible for what happened, often in a hidden way. People use it when they suspect someone had influence: Jeg tror, at han havde en finger med i spillet (I think he had a hand in it).

forms.da: Han har en finger med i spillet
Hun havde en finger med i spillet
forms.en: She had a hand in it

forms.da: Har du en finger med i spillet?

sentence.da: Politiet tror, at flere kan **have en finger med i spillet**.
sentence.en: The police think that several people may be involved.

at have en høne at plukke med nogen.explanation: "At have en høne at plukke med nogen" means "to have a bone to pick with someone": to be upset with a person and want to talk it through. The Danish picture is a hen to pluck. Name the person after med: Jeg har en høne at plukke med dig (I have a bone to pick with you).

forms.da: Jeg har en høne at plukke med dig
forms.en: I have a bone to pick with you

forms.da: Har du en høne at plukke med ham?
forms.en: Do you have a bone to pick with him?

forms.da: Hun havde en høne at plukke med sin bror
forms.en: She had a bone to pick with her brother

sentence.da: Det er svært at **have en høne at plukke med nogen**, man holder af.
sentence.en: It is hard to have a bone to pick with someone you love.

at have fri.explanation: "At have fri" means "to be off work", or off school: Børnene har fri i dag (The children are off today). To choose to take a day off, say at holde fri (to take time off).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **have fri** på mandag.
sentence.en: I would like to have Monday off.

at have fødselsdag.explanation: "At have fødselsdag" means "to have a birthday", and it is how you say it is your birthday: Jeg har fødselsdag i dag (It is my birthday today). To congratulate someone, say Tillykke med fødselsdagen! (Happy birthday!).

sentence.da: Min bror skal **have fødselsdag** i morgen.
sentence.en: My brother's birthday is tomorrow.

at have god tid.explanation: "At have god tid" means "to have plenty of time": Vi har god tid, før toget går (We have plenty of time before the train leaves). If you are in a hurry, say at have travlt (to be in a hurry).

forms.en: I have had plenty of time

sentence.da: Vi skal tage afsted tidligt for at **have god tid**.
sentence.en: We have to leave early to have plenty of time.

at have hjertet på rette sted.explanation: "At have hjertet på rette sted" means "to have one's heart in the right place", to have good intentions. People say it about someone who makes a mistake or acts clumsily, to show they do not hold it against them.

forms.da: Han har hjertet på rette sted.
forms.en: He has his heart in the right place.

forms.da: Hun er klodset, men hun har hjertet på rette sted.
forms.en: She is clumsy, but her heart is in the right place.

forms.da: Jeg ved, at du har hjertet på rette sted.
forms.en: I know your heart is in the right place.

sentence.da: Det er vigtigt at **have hjertet på rette sted**, når man hjælper andre.
sentence.en: It is important to have your heart in the right place when you help others.

at have is i maven.explanation: "At have is i maven" means "to keep cool" or "to stay calm": to not hurry or panic when others are nervous, for example before a deadline or a hard match. The picture is ice in the stomach, which keeps you cool. It is often said as advice: Man skal have is i maven (You have to keep your cool).

sentence.da: Før eksamen er det vigtigt at **have is i maven**.
sentence.en: Before the exam it is important to keep your cool.

at have let ved.explanation: "At have let ved" means "to find it easy to": Hun har let ved at lære sprog (She finds it easy to learn languages). For the opposite, say at have svært ved (to find it hard to).

forms.en: I have found it easy to

sentence.da: Han kan **have let ved** at tegne, fordi han øver sig meget.
sentence.en: He can find it easy to draw because he practices a lot.

at have lyst til.explanation: "At have lyst til" means "to feel like", or "to want to", and is followed by a thing or at + verb: Jeg har lyst til kaffe (I feel like coffee). Jeg har lyst til at gå en tur (I feel like going for a walk).

forms.en: I have felt like / wanted to

sentence.da: Man kan **have lyst til** en kold drink, når det er varmt.
sentence.en: You can feel like a cold drink when it is hot.

at have mulighed for.explanation: "At have mulighed for" means "to have the opportunity to", so to be able to do something: Du har mulighed for at læse her (You have the chance to read here). For a simple "can", use kan (can): Jeg kan komme (I can come).

forms.en: I have had the opportunity to

sentence.da: Du skal **have mulighed for** at tale med chefen.
sentence.en: You should have the chance to talk to the boss.

at have noget imod.explanation: "At have noget imod" means "to mind" or "to object to". It is mostly used in questions and with ikke (not): Har du noget imod musik? (Do you mind music?) Jeg har ikke noget imod det (I do not mind that).

sentence.da: Jeg ville ikke **have noget imod** en kop te.
sentence.en: I would not mind a cup of tea.

at have ondt i.explanation: "At have ondt i" means "to have a pain in", and you use it to say a body part hurts. Put the body part after it: Jeg har ondt i hovedet (I have a headache) or ondt i maven (a stomach ache). Danish says the head where English says my head.

forms.en: I have had a pain in

sentence.da: Jeg kan **have ondt i** halsen i dag.
sentence.en: I may have a sore throat today.

at have på.explanation: "At have på" means "to wear", literally to have on: Hvad har du på? (What are you wearing?). Putting clothes on is a different phrase, at tage tøj på (literally take clothes on), and taking them off is at tage tøj af.

sentence.da: Du skal **have på** en jakke.
sentence.en: You have to wear a jacket.

at have ret.explanation: "At have ret" means "to be right", but Danish literally says to have right. Du har ret means "You are right". Do not use er (is, am) here.

sentence.da: Ja, du kan **have ret** i det.
sentence.en: Yes, you may be right about that.

at have råd til.explanation: "At have råd til" means "to afford": Jeg har ikke råd til en ny telefon (I cannot afford a new phone). Here råd is about money, not about advice (et råd).

forms.en: I have been able to afford

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **have råd til** en ny cykel.
sentence.en: I would like to be able to afford a new bike.

at have svært ved.explanation: "At have svært ved" means "to find it hard to": Jeg har svært ved at sove (I find it hard to sleep). It also works with a thing: Hun har svært ved matematik (She finds math hard).

forms.en: I have found it hard to

sentence.da: Jeg kan **have svært ved** at stå tidligt op.
sentence.en: I can find it hard to get up early.

at have tid til.explanation: "At have tid til" means "to have time for" something: Har du tid til en kop kaffe? (Do you have time for a cup of coffee?) Before a verb, add at: Jeg har tid til at læse (I have time to read).

sentence.da: Efter arbejde vil jeg **have tid til** børnene.
sentence.en: After work I want to have time for the children.

at have travlt.explanation: "At have travlt" means "to be busy" or "to be in a hurry". Danish uses have (have) where English uses be: Jeg har travlt is literally I have busy.

sentence.da: Før jul kan butikkerne **have travlt**.
sentence.en: Before Christmas the shops can be busy.

at havne.explanation: "At havne" means "to end up", to come to rest in a place or situation, often one that was not planned: Bolden havnede i søen (The ball ended up in the lake). It is built on en havn (a harbor), the place where ships finally come in.

sentence.da: Pakken kan **havne** hos naboen, hvis vi ikke er hjemme.
sentence.en: The package may end up at the neighbor's if we are not home.

at hedde.explanation: "At hedde" means "to be called", and it is how you give your name: Jeg hedder Anna means "My name is Anna". It is also used for things: Hvad hedder det på dansk? (What is that called in Danish?).

sentence.da: Vores nye hund skal **hedde** Max.
sentence.en: Our new dog is going to be called Max.

at helbrede.explanation: "At helbrede" means "to cure", to make a sick person well or to make an illness go away. Someone or something does the curing, such as a doctor or a medicine. When a cut closes by itself, use at hele (to heal) instead.

sentence.da: Man kan **helbrede** nogle sygdomme med den rigtige behandling.
sentence.en: Some illnesses can be cured with the right treatment.

at hele.explanation: "At hele" means "to heal": a cut or a hurt feeling gets better by itself over time. The thing heals on its own. When a doctor makes someone well, you say at helbrede (to cure).

sentence.da: Et brækket ben kan **hele** på seks uger.
sentence.en: A broken leg can heal in six weeks.

at henrette.explanation: "At henrette" means "to execute": to end someone's life as an official punishment. It is only used for the legal act. For killing in general, the word is at dræbe (to kill).

sentence.da: I nogle lande kan staten stadig **henrette** forbrydere.
sentence.en: In some countries the state can still execute criminals.

at hente.explanation: "At hente" means "to fetch" or "to pick up": you go somewhere and get a thing or a person. Jeg henter pakken på posten (I pick up the parcel at the post office).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **hente** børnene i skolen klokken tre.
sentence.en: I have to pick up the children at school at three o'clock.

at henvende sig.explanation: "At henvende sig" means "to contact" or "to turn to", to go to a person or office to request help or information. It is common on signs: Henvend dig i receptionen (Please go to the reception desk). For the person or office you use til: Jeg henvendte mig til kommunen (I contacted the municipality).

sentence.da: Man kan **henvende sig** til biblioteket, hvis man har spørgsmål.
sentence.en: You can turn to the library if you have questions.

at henvise.explanation: "At henvise" means "to refer", to send someone on to another person or place, with til after it. In a text it means to point to a source.

sentence.da: Lægen vil **henvise** mig til en specialist på sygehuset.
sentence.en: The doctor will refer me to a specialist at the hospital.

at heppe.explanation: "At heppe" means "to cheer (for a team)", to shout and encourage a team or a person. Use på after it: Vi hepper på Danmark (We are cheering for Denmark).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **heppe** på dig, når du løber maraton.
sentence.en: I will cheer for you when you run the marathon.

at hikke.explanation: "At hikke" means "to hiccup", to make a quick little sound in your throat that you cannot control. The sound itself is et hik (a hiccup).

sentence.da: Man begynder at **hikke**, når man drikker for hurtigt.
sentence.en: You start to hiccup when you drink too fast.

at hilse.explanation: "At hilse" means "to greet" or "to say hello". To greet a person, add på (on): Jeg hilser på naboen (I say hello to the neighbor). Hils ham fra mig! (Say hi to him from me!)

sentence.da: Man skal **hilse**, når man kommer ind i butikken.
sentence.en: You should say hello when you walk into the store.

at hilse på.explanation: "At hilse på" means "to say hello to", and is used when you are introduced to someone: Jeg vil gerne hilse på din mor (I would like to say hello to your mom).

forms.en: I have said hello to / met

sentence.da: Du skal **hilse på** gæsterne, når de kommer.
sentence.en: You have to greet the guests when they arrive.

at hindre.explanation: "At hindre" means "to prevent" or "to hinder", to keep something from happening or someone from doing something. The common way to say it is hindre + person + i at + action: Sneen hindrede os i at køre (The snow kept us from driving).

sentence.da: Et væltet træ kan **hindre** trafikken på landevejen.
sentence.en: A fallen tree can hinder traffic on the country road.

at hive.explanation: "At hive" means "to pull" or "to heave", to pull something up or toward you with a quick, strong movement. A particle changes it: at hive i (to tug at) is a pull on something, and at hive efter vejret (to gasp for breath) is a common idiom.

sentence.da: Fiskeren skal **hive** nettet op af vandet med begge hænder.
sentence.en: The fisherman has to pull the net out of the water with both hands.

at hjælpe.explanation: "At hjælpe" means "to help", making something easier for someone. Shop staff often ask Kan jeg hjælpe dig? (Can I help you?). Hjælp! (Help!) is what you call out in an emergency.

sentence.da: Lægen vil **hjælpe** den syge mand.
sentence.en: The doctor wants to help the sick man.

at hjælpe med.explanation: "At hjælpe med" means "to help with" something. After med (with) comes the task: hjælpe med lektierne (help with the homework). To say who you help, put the person right after hjælper: Jeg hjælper dig med maden (I help you with the food).

sentence.da: Min bror vil **hjælpe med** flytningen.
sentence.en: My brother wants to help with the move.

at hjælpe til.explanation: "At hjælpe til" means "to help out": Børnene hjælper til ved festen (The kids help out at the party). You do not say whom you help. For a person, say Jeg hjælper min mor (I help my mom).

sentence.da: Vil du **hjælpe til** i køkkenet i aften?
sentence.en: Do you want to help out in the kitchen tonight?

at holde.explanation: "At holde" means "to hold" or "to keep": you have something in your hands, or you do not give it up. Hun holder en kop kaffe (She is holding a cup of coffee). Du må holde den (You can keep it). Holde en fest means "to throw a party".

sentence.da: Kan du **holde** min taske et øjeblik?
sentence.en: Can you hold my bag for a moment?

at holde af.explanation: "At holde af" means "to be fond of", a warm and gentle feeling for a person or thing: Jeg holder af min mormor (I am fond of my grandma).

sentence.da: Man kan **holde af** en ven uden at elske ham.
sentence.en: You can be fond of a friend without loving him.

at holde et løfte.explanation: "At holde et løfte" means "to keep a promise": Han holdt sit løfte (He kept his promise). The opposite is at bryde et løfte (to break a promise).

sentence.da: Man skal altid **holde et løfte**.
sentence.en: You must always keep a promise.

at holde fast.explanation: "At holde fast" means "to hold on", gripping tightly: Hold fast i rælingen! (Hold on to the railing!) It can also mean sticking to an idea: Han holder fast i sin mening (He sticks to his opinion).

sentence.da: Du skal **holde fast**, når bussen kører.
sentence.en: You must hold on when the bus is moving.

at holde ferie.explanation: "At holde ferie" means "to be on vacation": Vi holder ferie i juli (We are on vacation in July). For just one day off, use at tage fri (to take time off).

sentence.da: Vi vil **holde ferie** ved havet i år.
sentence.en: We want to be on vacation by the sea this year.

at holde fest.explanation: "At holde fest" means "to throw a party": Jeg holder fest i aften (I am throwing a party tonight). To go to one, say at tage til fest: Han tager til fest (He is going to a party).

sentence.da: Vi vil **holde fest** i haven på lørdag.
sentence.en: We want to throw a party in the garden on Saturday.

at holde fri.explanation: "At holde fri" means "to take time off", as a choice you make: Jeg holder fri på fredag (I am taking Friday off). To simply be off, say at have fri (to be off work).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **holde fri**, fordi jeg skal til lægen.
sentence.en: I want to take time off because I am going to the doctor.

at holde i hånd.explanation: "At holde i hånd" means "to hold hands": Vi holder i hånd på gåture (We hold hands on walks). Danish literally says i hånd (in hand) in the singular, even for two people.

sentence.da: Børnene skal **holde i hånd**, når de krydser vejen.
sentence.en: The children must hold hands when they cross the road.

at holde med.explanation: "At holde med" means "to support" a team or side, meaning you want it to win: Jeg holder med Danmark (I support Denmark).

forms.en: I have supported (a team or side)

sentence.da: Jeg plejer at **holde med** det danske hold.
sentence.en: I usually support the Danish team.

at holde møde.explanation: "At holde møde" means "to have a meeting". Danish uses holde (hold) here, not have: Vi holder møde klokken ti (We have a meeting at ten o'clock).

sentence.da: Vi skal **holde møde** i morgen tidlig.
sentence.en: We are having a meeting tomorrow morning.

at holde op.explanation: "At holde op" means "to stop", for ending something you were doing: Det holdt op med at regne (It stopped raining). With another action, add med at: Hun holdt op med at synge (She stopped singing).

sentence.da: Musikken skal **holde op** klokken ti.
sentence.en: The music has to stop at ten o'clock.

at holde op med.explanation: "At holde op med" means "to stop doing": Jeg holder op med at ryge (I am quitting smoking). Alone, holde op means "to stop": Regnen holder op (The rain stops).

sentence.da: Du skal **holde op med** at råbe.
sentence.en: You have to stop yelling.

at holde oplæg.explanation: "At holde oplæg" means "to give a presentation", to speak to a group about a topic, for example at work or in class. Danish uses holde (to hold) where English says give, so the same verb works for other talks: at holde en tale (to give a speech).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **holde oplæg** om mit projekt for hele klassen.
sentence.en: I am going to give a presentation about my project to the whole class.

at holde ord.explanation: "At holde ord" means "to keep one's word", to do what you promised. Danish uses no word for his or her here: Hun holder altid ord (She always keeps her word).

sentence.da: Når du har lovet noget, skal du **holde ord**.
sentence.en: When you have promised something, you must keep your word.

at holde pause.explanation: "At holde pause" means "to take a break": Vi holder pause klokken ti (We take a break at ten). Another way is at tage en pause: Jeg tager en pause (I am taking a break).

sentence.da: Vi skal **holde pause**, fordi vi er trætte.
sentence.en: We have to take a break because we are tired.

at holde sammen.explanation: "At holde sammen" means "to stick together": Familien holder sammen (The family sticks together). It also fits things that stay in one piece: Kagen holder ikke sammen (The cake does not hold together).

sentence.da: I svære tider skal vi **holde sammen**.
sentence.en: In hard times, we must stick together.

at holde sig.explanation: "At holde sig" means "to keep" or "to stay" in a certain state, such as warm, fit or calm. Hold dig varm (Stay warm). Han holder sig i form (He keeps himself fit). Jeg holder mig rolig (I stay calm).

sentence.da: Børnene skal **holde sig** væk fra ilden.
sentence.en: The children must stay away from the fire.

at holde sig i form.explanation: "At holde sig i form" means "to stay in shape": Han løber for at holde sig i form (He runs to stay in shape). Sig (oneself) changes with the person: Du holder dig i form (You stay in shape).

forms.da: jeg har holdt mig i form

sentence.da: Man skal **holde sig i form**, når man bliver ældre.
sentence.en: You have to stay in shape as you get older.

at holde styr på.explanation: "At holde styr på" means "to keep track of", so nothing gets lost: Hun holder styr på alle aftaler (She keeps track of all appointments). To watch over someone, use at holde øje med (to keep an eye on).

sentence.da: Det er svært at **holde styr på** alle børnene.
sentence.en: It is hard to keep track of all the kids.

at holde tale.explanation: "At holde tale" means "to give a speech": Han holdt en kort tale (He gave a short speech). Danish uses holde (to hold) for speeches.

sentence.da: Min chef vil **holde tale** ved festen.
sentence.en: My boss wants to give a speech at the party.

at holde tand for tunge.explanation: "At holde tand for tunge" means "to keep quiet": to say nothing about something, for example a surprise or a harsh remark. The picture is holding a tooth in front of the tongue to stop it from speaking. You do it on purpose, to avoid saying something you might regret.

sentence.da: Du må **holde tand for tunge** og ikke sige noget om gaven.
sentence.en: You must keep quiet and not say anything about the present.

at holde øje med.explanation: "At holde øje med" means "to keep an eye on", watching over someone or something: Hun holder øje med hunden (She keeps an eye on the dog).

forms.en: I have kept an eye on

sentence.da: Kan du **holde øje med** min taske?
sentence.en: Can you keep an eye on my bag?

at hoppe.explanation: "At hoppe" means "to jump", for example into water, over a puddle or on a trampoline. Add a small word to show the direction: hoppe op (jump up), hoppe ned (jump down) and hoppe i (jump in).

sentence.da: Børnene vil **hoppe** i vandet.
sentence.en: The children want to jump into the water.

at hoste.explanation: "At hoste" means "to cough", pushing air out of your throat with a sudden noise, often when you are sick. Jeg hoster meget (I cough a lot).

sentence.da: Jeg er syg og må **hoste** hele natten.
sentence.en: I am sick and have to cough all night.

at hugge.explanation: "At hugge" means "to chop", to cut something hard with heavy blows, for example wood. It is a forceful cut, unlike at skære (to cut with a knife).

sentence.da: Man bruger en økse til at **hugge** træ.
sentence.en: You use an axe to chop wood.

at hulke.explanation: "At hulke" means "to sob": to cry so hard that your chest shakes and your breath catches. It is a heavier crying than ordinary at græde (to cry).

sentence.da: Efter nyheden om ulykken begyndte hun at **hulke**.
sentence.en: After the news of the accident she began to sob.

at huske.explanation: "At huske" means "to remember", both to recall something and to remember to do something. Husk at ringe means "Remember to call". At huske på means "to keep in mind".

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **huske** hans navn.
sentence.en: I can't remember his name.

at huske på.explanation: "At huske på" means "to keep in mind": Husk på, at det er farligt (Keep in mind that it is dangerous). Plain at huske (to remember) is about recalling something. Adding på (on) is about not losing sight of it.

sentence.da: Du skal **huske på**, at vejen er glat.
sentence.en: You must keep in mind that the road is slippery.

at hvile.explanation: "At hvile" means "to rest", to stop being active so your body can recover: Hunden hviler i skyggen (The dog rests in the shade). To say that you rest yourself, Danes add sig: Jeg hviler mig lidt (I'm resting a bit).

sentence.da: Du bør **hvile** benet i en uge.
sentence.en: You should rest your leg for a week.

at hvile sig.explanation: "At hvile sig" means "to rest" after something tiring: Jeg hviler mig efter arbejde (I rest after work). To relax and do nothing in particular, use at slappe af (to relax): Jeg slapper af i sofaen (I relax on the sofa).

sentence.da: Han er træt og vil **hvile sig** lidt.
sentence.en: He is tired and wants to rest a little.

at hviske.explanation: "At hviske" means "to whisper", to speak in a very soft voice so that only someone close can hear: Vi hvisker i biblioteket (We whisper in the library).

sentence.da: Hun vil **hviske** en hemmelighed i mit øre.
sentence.en: She wants to whisper a secret in my ear.

at hygge sig.explanation: "At hygge sig" means "to have a cozy, nice time": Vi hygger os med film og kaffe (We are having a cozy time with movies and coffee). To wish someone that, say Hyg dig! (Have a nice time!)

forms.en: to have a cozy / nice time
I have a cozy / nice time
I had a cozy / nice time
I have had a cozy / nice time

sentence.da: Familien vil **hygge sig** ved bålet i aften.
sentence.en: The family wants to have a cozy time by the fire tonight.

at hylde.explanation: "At hylde" means "to honor" or "to celebrate": to say in public that someone has done something great, often with applause or a speech. For a birthday or a holiday, use at fejre (to celebrate).

sentence.da: Hele byen vil **hylde** holdet, der vandt pokalen.
sentence.en: The whole town wants to honor the team that won the cup.

at hyle.explanation: "At hyle" means "to howl", to make a long, loud, wailing sound. It is used for wolves and dogs, and also for wind: Vinden hyler om huset (The wind howls around the house).

sentence.da: Ulve kan **hyle** højt, når det er nat.
sentence.en: Wolves can howl loudly when it is night.

at hyre.explanation: "At hyre" means "to hire", to pay someone for their work: Vi hyrer en maler (We are hiring a painter). It also fits renting a boat or equipment for a short time. For a car or an apartment, Danes say at leje (to rent).

sentence.da: Vi skal **hyre** en tømrer til at bygge huset.
sentence.en: We must hire a carpenter to build the house.

at håbe.explanation: "At håbe" means "to hope", wanting something good to happen. Jeg håber, det går godt (I hope it goes well). To name the thing you hope for, add på (on): håbe på en gave (hope for a gift).

sentence.da: Vi må **håbe** på godt vejr i morgen.
sentence.en: We must hope for good weather tomorrow.

at håndtere.explanation: "At håndtere" means "to handle", to deal with a problem, a task or a person: Hun håndterer stress godt (She handles stress well). It contains hånd (hand), but it is mostly about dealing with something, not touching it.

sentence.da: Læreren kan **håndtere** en stor klasse uden problemer.
sentence.en: The teacher can handle a big class without problems.

at hælde.explanation: "At hælde" means "to pour" and "to lean": Jeg hælder mælk i glasset (I pour milk into the glass). Something can also slope: Taget hælder (The roof slopes).

sentence.da: Du skal **hælde** langsomt, når kanden er fuld.
sentence.en: You have to pour slowly when the pitcher is full.

at hænge.explanation: "At hænge" means "to hang", for something that is hanging: Billedet hænger på væggen (The picture hangs on the wall). Hænge ud means "to hang out": Vi hænger ud efter skole (We hang out after school).

sentence.da: Jakken skal **hænge** på knagen.
sentence.en: The jacket should hang on the hook.

at hænge op.explanation: "At hænge op" means "to hang up", on a hook, a wall or a line. Op adds the idea of up, and it goes after the thing you hang: Han hænger jakken op (He hangs the jacket up).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **hænge op**, når vaskemaskinen er færdig.
sentence.en: I have to hang up the laundry when the washing machine is done.

at hænge sammen.explanation: "At hænge sammen" means "to be connected" or "to make sense": Alt hænger sammen (Everything is connected). Historien hænger ikke sammen (The story does not make sense).

forms.en: it has made sense / been connected

sentence.da: Hans forklaring vil ikke **hænge sammen**.
sentence.en: His explanation will not make sense.

at hævde.explanation: "At hævde" means "to claim", to say that something is true, often when others doubt it: Han hævder, at han var hjemme (He claims that he was at home). To state a plain fact, use at sige (to say).

sentence.da: Tyven vil **hævde**, at han ikke var der.
sentence.en: The thief will claim that he was not there.

at hævde sig.explanation: "At hævde sig" means "to assert oneself": to show what you can do and make people respect you, for example at work or in sport. Without sig, at hævde means "to claim": Han hævder, at han er uskyldig (He claims he is innocent).

related.da: at stå op for sig selv

sentence.da: Den unge spiller vil gerne **hævde sig** på landsholdet.
sentence.en: The young player would like to assert himself on the national team.

at hæve.explanation: "At hæve" means "to raise", for example a price, a flag or your voice, and also "to withdraw" money from your account. Both uses are in these phrases: hæve prisen (raise the price) and hæve penge (withdraw money).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **hæve** penge i banken i morgen.
sentence.en: I must withdraw money at the bank tomorrow.

at hæve penge.explanation: "At hæve penge" means "to withdraw money", for example at an ATM: Jeg hæver penge i dag (I am withdrawing money today). The opposite is at sætte penge ind (to deposit money).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **hæve penge**, men banken er lukket.
sentence.en: I want to withdraw money, but the bank is closed.

at hævne.explanation: "At hævne" means "to avenge", to get back at someone for a wrong that was done. You avenge a person or a wrong: hævne sin bror (avenge his brother). To take revenge yourself, say at hævne sig (to take revenge).

sentence.da: Han vil **hævne** sin bror, som blev såret.
sentence.en: He wants to avenge his brother, who was hurt.

at høre.explanation: "At høre" means "to hear": Jeg hører en lyd (I hear a sound). It is also used for getting news: Jeg har hørt, at han flytter (I have heard that he is moving). For listening on purpose, use at lytte (to listen).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **høre** dig.
sentence.en: I cannot hear you.

at høre efter.explanation: "At høre efter" means "to listen", paying attention rather than just hearing sound: Hør efter, hvad jeg siger (Listen to what I say). Plain at høre means "to hear": Jeg hører musik (I hear music).

sentence.da: Børnene skal **høre efter**, når læreren taler.
sentence.en: The children must listen when the teacher speaks.

at høre fra.explanation: "At høre fra" means "to hear from" someone who contacts you: Jeg har ikke hørt fra Mette (I have not heard from Mette). For news about something, say at høre om: Jeg hørte om ulykken (I heard about the accident).

sentence.da: Jeg håber at **høre fra** dig snart.
sentence.en: I hope to hear from you soon.

at høre om.explanation: "At høre om" means "to hear about" something: Jeg hørte om ulykken i radioen (I heard about the accident on the radio).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **høre om** din rejse.
sentence.en: I would like to hear about your trip.

at høre til.explanation: "At høre til" means "to belong", being part of a place or group: Jeg hører til her (I belong here). Den hører til i skabet (It belongs in the cupboard).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **høre til** i gruppen.
sentence.en: I would like to belong to the group.

at høste.explanation: "At høste" means "to harvest", to gather crops like grain or fruit when they are ripe. It also works for results: høste anerkendelse (to earn recognition).

sentence.da: Bonden vil **høste** kornet, når det er modent.
sentence.en: The farmer will harvest the grain when it is ripe.

en hage.explanation: "En hage" means "a chin", the lower tip of the face. Danes call a double chin en dobbelthage.

sentence.da: Din **hage** sidder lige under munden.
sentence.en: Your chin is right under the mouth.

en hagesmæk.explanation: "En hagesmæk" means "a bib", worn under a baby's chin to keep clothes clean.

sentence.da: Babyen spiser grød med en **hagesmæk** på.
sentence.en: The baby eats porridge with a bib on.

en haj.explanation: "En haj" means "a shark", a large sea fish. The word is also used for people: en lånehaj (a loan shark) lends money at a very high cost.

sentence.da: En **haj** har skarpe tænder og bor i havet.
sentence.en: A shark has sharp teeth and lives in the sea.

en hakkebøf.explanation: "En hakkebøf" means "a hamburger steak", a flat patty of ground beef fried in a pan. It is a classic Danish dinner, eaten with brown gravy and not in a bun.

sentence.da: Til aftensmad fik vi **hakkebøf** med bløde løg og kartofler.
sentence.en: For dinner we had hamburger steak with soft onions and potatoes.

en hal.explanation: "En hal" means "a hall", a big room or building, often for sports. It does not mean the hallway in a home. That is en gang (a hallway): Skoene står i gangen (The shoes are in the hallway).

sentence.da: En **hal** er et stort rum med plads til mange.
sentence.en: A hall is a big room with space for many people.

en hale.explanation: "En hale" means "a tail", the part at the back of an animal's body.

sentence.da: Hunden logrer med sin **hale**, når den er glad.
sentence.en: The dog wags its tail when it is happy.

en halmballe.explanation: "En halmballe" means "a straw bale". It is built from halm (straw) and balle (bale), and farmers use the bales as bedding in animal stalls.

sentence.da: En **halmballe** er tørre strå, der er presset tæt sammen.
sentence.en: A straw bale is dry stalks that are pressed tightly together.

en hals.explanation: "En hals" means both "a neck" and "a throat", because Danish has one word for both. Jeg har ondt i halsen means "I have a sore throat". A necklace is en halskæde (a neck chain).

sentence.da: Hun har en smuk kæde om sin **hals**.
sentence.en: She has a pretty chain around her neck.

en halsbetændelse.explanation: "En halsbetændelse" means "a throat infection", a sore throat caused by germs. A plain sore throat is ondt i halsen (pain in the throat): Jeg har ondt i halsen (My throat hurts).

sentence.da: Hun har **halsbetændelse** og må blive hjemme.
sentence.en: She has a throat infection and has to stay home.

en halsedisse.explanation: "En halsedisse" means "a neck warmer", a soft tube of cloth that you pull over your head and neck.

sentence.da: Jeg tager en **halsedisse** på, når det blæser.
sentence.en: I put on a neck warmer when it is windy.

en halskæde.explanation: "En halskæde" means "a necklace", jewelry worn around the neck. It is built from hals (neck) and kæde (chain). Hals also means throat: Jeg har ondt i halsen (I have a sore throat).

sentence.da: Hun har en **halskæde** om halsen.
sentence.en: She has a necklace around her neck.

en halspastil.explanation: "En halspastil" means "a throat lozenge", built from hals (throat) and pastil (lozenge). You take one for a cough.

sentence.da: Jeg tager en **halspastil**, når min hals gør ondt.
sentence.en: I take a throat lozenge when my throat hurts.

en halv time.explanation: "En halv time" means "half an hour". Be careful with clock times: halv fem means 4:30, not 5:30, because it is half an hour before five.

sentence.da: Bussen kommer om **en halv time**.
sentence.en: The bus comes in half an hour.

en halvbror.explanation: "En halvbror" means "a half-brother", a brother who shares only one parent with you.

sentence.da: Han er min **halvbror**, fordi vi har samme far.
sentence.en: He is my half-brother because we have the same father.

en halvdel.explanation: "En halvdel" means "a half", one of two equal parts. Before another word, use halv: en halv pizza (half a pizza).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser den ene **halvdel** af kagen.
sentence.en: I eat one half of the cake.

en halvleg.explanation: "En halvleg" means "a half" of a game such as football or handball: første halvleg (the first half). For a half of anything else, use en halvdel (a half of something).

sentence.da: Første **halvleg** sluttede nul-nul, men vi scorede efter pausen.
sentence.en: The first half ended nil-nil, but we scored after the break.

en halvsøster.explanation: "En halvsøster" means "a half-sister", a sister who shares only one parent with you.

sentence.da: Hun er min **halvsøster**, fordi vi har samme mor.
sentence.en: She is my half-sister because we have the same mother.

en halvø.explanation: "En halvø" means "a peninsula", land with water on most sides but joined to larger land. It is built from halv (half) and ø (island). An island has water on all sides: Fyn er en ø (Funen is an island).

sentence.da: Jylland er en **halvø** og hænger sammen med Tyskland.
sentence.en: Jutland is a peninsula and is joined to Germany.

en hammer.explanation: "En hammer" means "a hammer", a tool with a heavy metal head. Use a hammer for nails and en skruetrækker (a screwdriver) for screws.

sentence.da: Han slår sømmet i med en **hammer**.
sentence.en: He hits the nail in with a hammer.

en hamster.explanation: "En hamster" means "a hamster", a small pet that lives in a cage.

sentence.da: Min **hamster** sover om dagen og løber om natten.
sentence.en: My hamster sleeps during the day and runs around at night.

en handel.explanation: "En handel" means "a deal" or "a trade", something two sides agree on. Without en, handel means trade in general: Handel mellem lande (Trade between countries).

sentence.da: Det var en god **handel** for os begge.
sentence.en: That was a good deal for both of us.

en handling.explanation: "En handling" means "an action", something a person does. It is also the plot of a story: Filmens handling er enkel (The plot of the film is simple).

sentence.da: Hans **handling** var meget modig.
sentence.en: His action was very brave.

en handske.explanation: "En handske" means "a glove", with a separate part for each finger. Do not mix it up with en vante (a mitten), which has one part for the thumb and one for the other fingers.

sentence.da: Jeg har en **handske** på hånden.
sentence.en: I have a glove on my hand.

en hane.explanation: "En hane" means "a rooster", the male chicken. It also means "a faucet" on a sink: Luk for hanen (Turn off the faucet).

sentence.da: En **hane** galer tidligt om morgenen.
sentence.en: A rooster crows early in the morning.

en harddisk.explanation: "En harddisk" means "a hard drive", the part of a computer where your files are stored.

sentence.da: Min **harddisk** er fuld af gamle billeder.
sentence.en: My hard drive is full of old photos.

en hare.explanation: "En hare" means "a hare", a fast wild animal with long ears. A pet rabbit is en kanin, not en hare.

sentence.da: En **hare** kan løbe meget hurtigt.
sentence.en: A hare can run very fast.

en harmoni.explanation: "En harmoni" means "a harmony", a state where things fit together without conflict: at leve i harmoni med naturen (to live in harmony with nature). In music, it is notes that sound good together.

sentence.da: Familien lever i **harmoni**, og der er sjældent skænderier.
sentence.en: The family lives in harmony, and there are rarely quarrels.

en hasselnød.explanation: "En hasselnød" means "a hazelnut", built from hassel (hazel) and nød (nut). Nød also names a small Danish spice treat, en pebernød (a small spice treat), so it does not always mean a nut.

sentence.da: En **hasselnød** er en lille nød med hård skal.
sentence.en: A hazelnut is a small nut with a hard shell.

en hastighed.explanation: "En hastighed" means "a speed", often on the road. In everyday talk, Danes also say fart (speed): høj fart (high speed).

sentence.da: Du kører med for høj **hastighed**.
sentence.en: You are driving at too high a speed.

en hat.explanation: "En hat" means "a hat", usually one with a brim, like a sun hat. It is not the same as en hue (a warm knitted cap) or en kasket (a cap with a peak).

sentence.da: Hun har en stor **hat** på hovedet.
sentence.en: She has a big hat on her head.

en have.explanation: "En have" means "a garden". Do not mix it up with at have (to have), which is spelled the same. I haven means "in the garden".

sentence.da: Vi har en **have** med blomster og træer.
sentence.en: We have a garden with flowers and trees.

en havefest.explanation: "En havefest" means "a garden party", a party held outside in someone's garden. It is built from have (garden) and fest (party). Do not mix en have (a garden) with at have (to have): Jeg har en have (I have a garden).

sentence.da: Til vores **havefest** sidder vi ude og griller.
sentence.en: At our garden party, we sit outside and grill.

en haveslange.explanation: "En haveslange" means "a garden hose". It is built from have (garden) and slange (hose, also snake). Context tells which one you mean: Slangen bed ham (The snake bit him) is the animal.

sentence.da: Han vasker bilen med en **haveslange**.
sentence.en: He washes the car with a garden hose.

en havestol.explanation: "En havestol" means "a garden chair", a chair for sitting outside. It is have (garden) plus stol (chair). Have starts many garden words, such as en haveslange (a garden hose).

sentence.da: Jeg sidder i en **havestol** og drikker kaffe.
sentence.en: I sit in a garden chair and drink coffee.

en havfrue.explanation: "En havfrue" means "a mermaid", a creature from old tales and sea stories. It is built from hav (sea) and frue (lady).

sentence.da: I eventyret har en **havfrue** en fiskehale i stedet for ben.
sentence.en: In the story, a mermaid has a fish tail instead of legs.

en havn.explanation: "En havn" means "a harbor" or "a port", the place where ships and boats stay. The same word is used for a small boat harbor and a big port.

sentence.da: Der er mange både i en lille **havn**.
sentence.en: There are many boats in a small harbor.

en havnebus.explanation: "En havnebus" means "a harbor bus", a boat that carries passengers across the water, like a bus.

sentence.da: Vi tager en **havnebus** over vandet, og det tager ti minutter.
sentence.en: We take a harbor bus across the water, and it takes ten minutes.

en havnepromenade.explanation: "En havnepromenade" means "a harbor promenade", a wide path along the water where people stroll, jog and sit outside. It is built from havn (harbor) and promenade (promenade).

sentence.da: Der ligger caféer og isbarer langs den nye **havnepromenade**.
sentence.en: There are cafés and ice cream bars along the new harbor promenade.

en hede.explanation: "En hede" means "a heath / moor", wide open land with sandy soil, almost no trees and heather. Large heaths are found in western Jutland.

sentence.da: På en **hede** er jorden sandet, og der vokser næsten ingen træer.
sentence.en: On a heath the soil is sandy, and almost no trees grow.

en hedebølge.explanation: "En hedebølge" means "a heat wave", several days in a row of unusually hot weather. It uses bølge (wave) like en kuldebølge (a cold snap).

sentence.da: Under en **hedebølge** er det næsten for varmt til at sove.
sentence.en: During a heat wave it is almost too hot to sleep.

en heks.explanation: "En heks" means "a witch", like in children's stories. It is also an insult for a mean woman, as in English.

sentence.da: Børnene var bange for den onde **heks**.
sentence.en: The children were afraid of the evil witch.

en helhed.explanation: "En helhed" means "a whole", something seen as one complete thing and not as separate pieces. A common phrase is i sin helhed (as a whole): Vi har læst bogen i sin helhed (We have read the book as a whole).

sentence.da: Delene passer sammen, og de danner en **helhed**.
sentence.en: The pieces fit together, and they form a whole.

en helikopter.explanation: "En helikopter" means "a helicopter", a flying machine that can hover in one place and land almost anywhere.

sentence.da: En **helikopter** har blade og letter lige op i luften.
sentence.en: A helicopter has blades and takes off straight up into the air.

en helligdag.explanation: "En helligdag" means "a public holiday", a day when most people do not work and many shops are closed. It is built from hellig (holy) and dag (day). Opening hours often say lukket søn- og helligdage (closed on Sundays and public holidays).

sentence.da: Juledag er en **helligdag**, og vi har fri.
sentence.en: Christmas Day is a public holiday, and we have the day off.

en hemmelighed.explanation: "En hemmelighed" means "a secret": Kan du holde en hemmelighed? (Can you keep a secret?). The describing word is hemmelig (secret): en hemmelig plan (a secret plan).

sentence.da: Det er en **hemmelighed**, og ingen må vide det.
sentence.en: It is a secret, and nobody may know.

en hensigt.explanation: "En hensigt" means "an intention", what you mean to do. The usual phrase is at have til hensigt at (to intend to): Jeg har til hensigt at flytte (I intend to move). It sounds a bit formal, and in everyday speech Danes say Jeg vil flytte (I want to move).

sentence.da: Min **hensigt** var ikke at såre dig.
sentence.en: My intention was not to hurt you.

en henvendelse.explanation: "En henvendelse" means "an inquiry", when you contact a company or authority with a question or a wish. A typical line from customer service is Tak for din henvendelse (Thank you for contacting us).

sentence.da: Vi besvarer din **henvendelse** inden for to hverdage.
sentence.en: We will answer your inquiry within two working days.

en henvisning.explanation: "En henvisning" means "a referral / reference". At the family doctor, it is the paper that sends you on to a hospital or another doctor. In writing, it points the reader to where to find more information.

sentence.da: Du skal bruge en **henvisning** fra lægen for at komme på sygehuset.
sentence.en: You need a referral from the doctor to get into the hospital.

en herre.explanation: "En herre" means "a gentleman", and also "a lord" or "a master". On a restroom sign, Herrer (Men) is the men's room.

sentence.da: Den høje **herre** dér venter på dig.
sentence.en: That tall gentleman over there is waiting for you.

en hersker.explanation: "En hersker" means "a ruler", a person who holds the highest power over a country or a people, especially in history. The word does not say whether the person was good or bad.

sentence.da: Den, der styrer hele landet alene, er en **hersker**.
sentence.en: The one who rules the whole country alone is a ruler.

en hest.explanation: "En hest" means "a horse", a large animal that people ride. At ride på hest means "to go horse riding", using at ride (to ride).

sentence.da: En **hest** spiser græs og løber hurtigt.
sentence.en: A horse eats grass and runs fast.

en hestehale.explanation: "En hestehale" means "a ponytail", hair tied together at the back of the head. It is built from hest (horse) and hale (tail), so it is literally a horse tail.

sentence.da: Hun har samlet håret i en høj **hestehale**.
sentence.en: She has gathered her hair in a high ponytail.

en hilsen.explanation: "En hilsen" means "a greeting", and also a friendly message you send to someone. At the end of a letter, Venlig hilsen (Kind regards) is common.

sentence.da: Jeg sender dig en **hilsen** fra Danmark.
sentence.en: I'm sending you a greeting from Denmark.

en himmel.explanation: "En himmel" means "a sky", and it can also mean "heaven". Danes usually say himlen (the sky) instead. Himlen er grå means "The sky is gray".

sentence.da: Der er mange stjerner på en mørk **himmel**.
sentence.en: There are many stars in a dark sky.

en hindbærsnitte.explanation: "En hindbærsnitte" means "a raspberry slice", a flat rectangular pastry sold in Danish bakeries. It is built from hindbær (raspberry) and snitte (slice).

sentence.da: Til kaffen fik vi en **hindbærsnitte** med syltetøj og glasur.
sentence.en: With the coffee we had a raspberry slice with jam and icing.

en hindring.explanation: "En hindring" means "an obstacle", anything that stops or slows you down. It can be something real on a road, but also something you cannot touch, like rules or fear.

sentence.da: Manglende sprogkundskaber kan være en stor **hindring** på et nyt job.
sentence.en: Missing language skills can be a big obstacle in a new job.

en hingst.explanation: "En hingst" means "a stallion", an adult male horse. A female is called en hoppe (a mare).

sentence.da: En **hingst** bruges til avl, så der kommer nye heste.
sentence.en: A stallion is used for breeding, so new horses are born.

en historie.explanation: "En historie" means both a story and history (the past, also the school subject), and the situation shows which. Fortæl en historie means "tell a story", and "Danmarks historie" means "the history of Denmark".

sentence.da: Han fortæller en sjov **historie**.
sentence.en: He tells a funny story.

en historiebog.explanation: "En historiebog" means "a history book", often a school textbook about the past. It is built from historie (history) and en bog (a book). Historie also means a story: en historie om en prins (a story about a prince).

sentence.da: I vores **historiebog** læser vi om vikingerne.
sentence.en: In our history book, we read about the Vikings.

en historiker.explanation: "En historiker" means "a historian", a person who studies and writes about the past, often at a university or museum. It is built on historie, which means both "history" and "story".

sentence.da: En **historiker** læser gamle breve for at forstå fortiden.
sentence.en: A historian reads old letters to understand the past.

en hjelm.explanation: "En hjelm" means "a helmet", worn to protect your head, for example when riding or on a building site.

sentence.da: Børn skal have **hjelm** på, når de cykler.
sentence.en: Children must wear a helmet when they bike.

en hjemmeopgave.explanation: "En hjemmeopgave" means "a homework assignment", one task you do at home for school or university. For everyday school homework in general, Danes say lektier (homework).

sentence.da: Læreren gav klassen en **hjemmeopgave** om Danmarks historie.
sentence.en: The teacher gave the class a homework assignment about Denmark's history.

en hjemmeside.explanation: "En hjemmeside" means "a website", the place on the internet where a person or a company shows information. It is built from hjemme (home) and side (page). Hjemme means at home, but hjem means toward home: Jeg er hjemme (I am at home), Jeg går hjem (I am going home).

sentence.da: Du kan se åbningstiderne på butikkens **hjemmeside**.
sentence.en: You can see the opening hours on the shop's website.

en hjemmesko.explanation: "En hjemmesko" means "a slipper". It is built from hjemme (at home) and sko (shoe), so it is literally a home shoe. You usually say et par hjemmesko (a pair of slippers), since you wear two.

sentence.da: Jeg har varme **hjemmesko** på i huset.
sentence.en: I am wearing warm slippers in the house.

en hjemrejse.explanation: "En hjemrejse" means "a return trip", the journey back home after being away. It is built from hjem (home) and rejse (trip). Rejse is also a verb: at rejse hjem (to travel home).

sentence.da: Efter ferien starter vores **hjemrejse** fra Spanien.
sentence.en: After the vacation, our trip home starts from Spain.

en hjerne.explanation: "En hjerne" means "a brain", the organ you think with. Hjernerystelse means "concussion".

sentence.da: Din **hjerne** sidder inde i hovedet.
sentence.en: Your brain sits inside the head.

en hjernerystelse.explanation: "En hjernerystelse" means "a concussion". After a hard hit to the head, the brain is shaken inside the skull, and you may feel dizzy or sick. It is built from hjerne (brain) and rystelse (shaking).

sentence.da: En **hjernerystelse** kommer af et hårdt slag mod hovedet.
sentence.en: A concussion comes from a hard blow to the head.

en hjort.explanation: "En hjort" means "a deer", the larger kind with antlers on the male. A smaller deer is et rådyr (a roe deer).

sentence.da: Vi så en **hjort** med et stort gevir.
sentence.en: We saw a deer with big antlers.

en hobby.explanation: "En hobby" means "a hobby", something you do for fun in your spare moments.

sentence.da: Min **hobby** er at male billeder.
sentence.en: My hobby is painting pictures.

en hofte.explanation: "En hofte" means "a hip", the place on each side of the body where the leg meets the body. It is also the joint there, so an older person may get en ny hofte (a new hip).

sentence.da: Din **hofte** sidder mellem taljen og låret.
sentence.en: Your hip sits between the waist and the thigh.

en holdbarhedsdato.explanation: "En holdbarhedsdato" means "a best-before date". It tells you how long food stays good.

sentence.da: Jeg tjekker altid mælkens **holdbarhedsdato**.
sentence.en: I always check the milk's best-before date.

en holdkammerat.explanation: "En holdkammerat" means "a teammate", someone on your sports team. It is built from hold (team) and kammerat (buddy). Kammerat is a friendly word for someone you do things with, so it also builds en legekammerat (a playmate).

sentence.da: Min **holdkammerat** og jeg spiller på samme hold.
sentence.en: My teammate and I play on the same team.

en holdning.explanation: "En holdning" means "an attitude", how you think about something: at have en holdning til noget (to have a view on something). It also means how you stand and sit, so en god holdning (good posture) is a straight back.

sentence.da: Hun har en klar **holdning** til, hvordan skolen skal drives.
sentence.en: She has a clear view on how the school should be run.

en honningkage.explanation: "En honningkage" means "a honey cake" or "gingerbread". It is built from honning (honey) and kage (cake). Kage is also used for small baked treats: en småkage is literally a small cake.

sentence.da: Vi bager en **honningkage** med honning og kanel.
sentence.en: We bake a honey cake with honey and cinnamon.

en hoppe.explanation: "En hoppe" means "a mare", an adult female horse. Do not mix it up with the verb at hoppe (to jump), which looks the same.

sentence.da: Når en **hoppe** får et føl, bliver hun mor.
sentence.en: When a mare has a foal, she becomes a mother.

en horisont.explanation: "En horisont" means "a horizon", both the far line you see at sea and the limits of what you know: at udvide sin horisont (to broaden your horizons).

sentence.da: En **horisont** er den linje, hvor himlen møder havet.
sentence.en: A horizon is the line where the sky meets the sea.

en hoste.explanation: "En hoste" means "a cough", the sudden noise you make when your throat is irritated, often from a cold. You can say Jeg har en hoste or Jeg har hoste, both meaning "I have a cough".

sentence.da: Med en **hoste** er det svært at sove.
sentence.en: With a cough, it is hard to sleep.

en hostesaft.explanation: "En hostesaft" means "a cough syrup", a sweet liquid medicine that you buy at a pharmacy and take with a spoon. It is built from hoste (cough) and saft (a thick, sweet drink).

sentence.da: Jeg tog en skefuld **hostesaft** mod min hoste.
sentence.en: I took a spoonful of cough syrup for my cough.

en hotdog.explanation: "En hotdog" means "a hot dog", a sausage in a bun. The sausage on its own is en pølse (a sausage).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en **hotdog** med pølse, brød og ketchup.
sentence.en: I eat a hot dog with sausage, bread and ketchup.

en hov.explanation: "En hov" means "a hoof", the hard part at the bottom of a horse's leg. Cows and pigs have a split hoof, which Danes call en klov (a cloven hoof).

sentence.da: Hesten har en hård **hov** på hver fod.
sentence.en: The horse has a hard hoof on each foot.

en hovedbanegård.explanation: "En hovedbanegård" means "a central station", the main and biggest train station in a city. It is built from hoved (main), bane (railway) and gård (yard). Hoved also means head: Jeg har ondt i hovedet (My head hurts).

sentence.da: København har en stor **hovedbanegård**.
sentence.en: Copenhagen has a big central station.

en hoveddør.explanation: "En hoveddør" means "a front door", the main door of a house or an apartment. It is built from hoved (main) and dør (door). Hoved also makes other main words, such as en hovedvej (a main road).

sentence.da: Vores **hoveddør** vender ud mod gaden.
sentence.en: Our front door faces the street.

en hovedgade.explanation: "En hovedgade" means "a main street", the biggest and busiest street in a town.

sentence.da: Der er mange butikker og caféer i byens **hovedgade**.
sentence.en: There are many shops and cafés on the town's main street.

en hovedingrediens.explanation: "En hovedingrediens" means "a main ingredient", what a dish is mostly made of, like the beef in a stew. Hoved- (literally "head") at the start of a word means "main": en hovedvej (a main road).

sentence.da: Æg er en **hovedingrediens** i pandekager, sammen med mel og mælk.
sentence.en: Eggs are a main ingredient in pancakes, together with flour and milk.

en hovedperson.explanation: "En hovedperson" means "a main character", the person a book, film or story is mostly about. The opposite is a person who only helps the story along.

sentence.da: Hun er **hovedperson** i filmen, så vi ser hende hele tiden.
sentence.en: She is the main character in the film, so we see her all the time.

en hovedpine.explanation: "En hovedpine" means "a headache". It is built from hoved (head) and pine (pain). Danes say Jeg har hovedpine (I have a headache) without en. Jeg har ondt i hovedet means the same, literally I have a pain in the head.

sentence.da: Jeg har **hovedpine** og tager en pille.
sentence.en: I have a headache and take a pill.

en hovedret.explanation: "En hovedret" means "a main course", the biggest dish of a meal. It is built from hoved (main) and ret (dish). Ret also appears on menus: dagens ret (the dish of the day).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser fisk som **hovedret**.
sentence.en: I eat fish for my main course.

en hovedrolle.explanation: "En hovedrolle" means "a leading role", the biggest role in a film or play. Use it with at spille (to play): at spille hovedrollen (to play the lead). The person in the story is a hovedperson (a main character).

sentence.da: Den unge pige fik en **hovedrolle** i den nye film.
sentence.en: The young girl got a leading role in the new film.

en hovedstad.explanation: "En hovedstad" means "a capital city". It is built from hoved (head) and stad (city). The same hoved (head) is in et hoved (a head) and en hovedperson (a main character).

sentence.da: København er Danmarks **hovedstad**.
sentence.en: Copenhagen is the capital of Denmark.

en hovmester.explanation: "En hovmester" means "a head waiter", the senior person who runs the dining room in a fine restaurant.

sentence.da: En **hovmester** byder gæsterne velkommen og viser dem hen til bordet.
sentence.en: A head waiter welcomes the guests and shows them to the table.

en hr-medarbejder.explanation: "En HR-medarbejder" means "an HR employee", someone who works with the people side of a company: finding new staff, contracts and questions from workers. Danes say HR letter by letter, like in English.

sentence.da: Vores **HR-medarbejder** hjælper med ansættelser og spørgsmål om løn.
sentence.en: Our HR employee helps with hiring and questions about pay.

en hudlæge.explanation: "En hudlæge" means "a dermatologist", a doctor for the skin. It is built from en hud (skin) and en læge (doctor). Hud also appears in en hudcreme (a skin cream).

sentence.da: Jeg har udslæt og skal til **hudlæge**.
sentence.en: I have a rash and am going to the dermatologist.

en hue.explanation: "En hue" means "a beanie", a knitted or woolen cap that keeps your head warm. It is different from en hat (a hat with a brim) and en kasket (a cap with a peak).

sentence.da: Jeg har en varm **hue** på hovedet.
sentence.en: I have a warm beanie on my head.

en hugorm.explanation: "En hugorm" means "an adder / viper", a snake with a dark zigzag line along its back. It lives on heaths and dunes, and its bite is painful but rarely dangerous to adults.

sentence.da: Den eneste giftige slange i Danmark er en **hugorm**.
sentence.en: The only venomous snake in Denmark is an adder.

en hukommelse.explanation: "En hukommelse" means "a memory", the ability to keep things in your mind. One memory of a trip or a day is et minde (a memory).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver ting ned, fordi min **hukommelse** er dårlig.
sentence.en: I write things down because my memory is bad.

en hule.explanation: "En hule" means "a cave", a natural hollow place in rock or a hill. It is also the den where a wild animal lives: Ræven bor i en hule (The fox lives in a den).

sentence.da: Flagermus sover om dagen i en mørk **hule**.
sentence.en: Bats sleep during the day in a dark cave.

en humlebi.explanation: "En humlebi" means "a bumblebee", a type of bee that lives in small groups, not in a big hive. Bi at the end of a word means bee.

sentence.da: En **humlebi** er rund og lodden og summer højt mellem blomsterne.
sentence.en: A bumblebee is round and furry and buzzes loudly between the flowers.

en hummer.explanation: "En hummer" means "a lobster", the sea animal with two big claws. When you mean the food, drop en: Vi bestiller hummer (We order lobster).

sentence.da: En **hummer** bor i havet og har store klør.
sentence.en: A lobster lives in the sea and has big claws.

en hund.explanation: "En hund" means "a dog", the animal that is often kept as a pet.

sentence.da: Min **hund** elsker at løbe efter katten.
sentence.en: My dog loves to run after the cat.

en hundeejer.explanation: "En hundeejer" means "a dog owner". It is built from hund (dog) and ejer (owner). Ejer also builds other owner words, such as en husejer (a homeowner).

sentence.da: Som **hundeejer** går jeg lange ture hver dag.
sentence.en: As a dog owner, I take long walks every day.

en hundekurv.explanation: "En hundekurv" means "a dog bed", the place where a dog sleeps. It is built from hund (dog) and kurv (basket). Kurv also means a basket on its own: en kurv med æbler (a basket of apples).

sentence.da: Vi har købt en blød **hundekurv** til vores hund.
sentence.en: We have bought a soft dog bed for our dog.

en hundelufter.explanation: "En hundelufter" means "a dog walker", a person who takes dogs out for a walk, sometimes as a job. It comes from at lufte hund (to walk a dog).

sentence.da: Vores **hundelufter** henter hunden klokken tolv.
sentence.en: Our dog walker picks up the dog at twelve o'clock.

en hundeskov.explanation: "En hundeskov" means "a dog park", a piece of woodland set aside for dogs. It is built from hund (dog) and skov (forest), so it feels like a small wood and not an open field.

sentence.da: Man må lukke hunden løs i en **hundeskov**.
sentence.en: You may let the dog off the leash in a dog park.

en hushjælp.explanation: "En hushjælp" means "a domestic helper", a person who helps with cleaning and housework at your home. It is built from hus (house) and hjælp (help). Hjælp also gives the verb at hjælpe (to help): Kan du hjælpe mig? (Can you help me?)

sentence.da: Vores **hushjælp** gør rent og vasker tøj.
sentence.en: Our domestic helper cleans and does laundry.

en husholdning.explanation: "En husholdning" means "a household", the people who live together and share the costs of living there. It also means running the daily life there, like cooking, cleaning and shopping.

sentence.da: De har fælles **husholdning** og deler alle udgifterne.
sentence.en: They have a shared household and split all the expenses.

en husmor.explanation: "En husmor" means "a housewife", a woman who stays home to care for the house and children: Min mor var husmor (My mother was a housewife). For a job like this, Danes leave out en.

sentence.da: En **husmor** passer hjemmet og børnene hele dagen.
sentence.en: A housewife looks after the home and the children all day.

en huspris.explanation: "En huspris" means "a house price", what a house costs to buy. It is mostly used in the plural: Huspriserne stiger (House prices are rising).

sentence.da: En høj **huspris** gør det svært for unge at købe bolig.
sentence.en: A high house price makes it hard for young people to buy a home.

en husregel.explanation: "En husregel" means "a house rule", a rule that everyone in a home or building must follow. The full written list is called en husorden (house rules).

sentence.da: Vores **husregel** er, at man tager skoene af.
sentence.en: Our house rule is that you take your shoes off.

en husstand.explanation: "En husstand" means "a household", all the people who live together in one home, counted as one unit. You see it in official forms and statistics: husstandens samlede indkomst (the household's total income).

sentence.da: Der bor fire personer i vores **husstand**.
sentence.en: Four people live in our household.

en hustru.explanation: "En hustru" means "a wife", but it is formal and a bit old-fashioned, as in Må jeg præsentere min hustru? (May I introduce my wife?). In everyday speech, Danes say kone: Det er min kone (That is my wife).

sentence.da: Han præsenterede sin **hustru** for gæsterne ved middagen.
sentence.en: He introduced his wife to the guests at dinner.

en hval.explanation: "En hval" means "a whale", the huge animal of the sea. It looks like a fish, but it is not.

sentence.da: En stor **hval** svømmer langt ude i havet.
sentence.en: A big whale swims far out in the sea.

en hvalp.explanation: "En hvalp" means "a puppy". The same word fits young foxes and wolves: en rævehvalp (a fox cub).

sentence.da: En **hvalp** bliver til en stor hund.
sentence.en: A puppy grows into a big dog.

en hvalros.explanation: "En hvalros" means "a walrus", a big sea animal of the Arctic. The first part looks like hval (whale), but a walrus is not a whale.

sentence.da: En **hvalros** har lange stødtænder og lever i det kolde Arktis.
sentence.en: A walrus has long tusks and lives in the cold Arctic.

en hveps.explanation: "En hveps" means "a wasp", an insect that often turns up around sweet food and drinks in summer. Do not mix it up with en bi (a bee), which is rounder and furrier.

sentence.da: En **hveps** er gul og sort og kan stikke.
sentence.en: A wasp is yellow and black and can sting.

en hverdag.explanation: "En hverdag" means "a weekday", Monday to Friday, and also "everyday life": Jeg arbejder om hverdagen (I work on weekdays). Hverdagen er travl (Everyday life is busy).

sentence.da: Lørdag er ikke en **hverdag**, men en weekend.
sentence.en: Saturday is not a weekday, but a weekend.

en hvidvin.explanation: "En hvidvin" means "a white wine". It is built from hvid (white) and vin (wine). Danish has no word for "of" here: et glas hvidvin means "a glass of white wine".

sentence.da: Jeg drikker et glas **hvidvin** til fisk.
sentence.en: I drink a glass of white wine with fish.

en hyld.explanation: "En hyld" means "an elder tree", a bush or small tree with white flowers in early summer and dark purple berries later. The flowers are used for hyldeblomstsaft (elderflower cordial), a typical Danish summer drink. Do not mix it up with en hylde (a shelf).

sentence.da: På en **hyld** vokser der hvide blomster, og senere mørke bær.
sentence.en: On an elder tree grow white flowers, and later dark berries.

en hylde.explanation: "En hylde" means "a shelf", a flat board on a wall or in a cabinet where you put things.

sentence.da: Tallerkenerne står på den øverste **hylde**.
sentence.en: The plates are on the top shelf.

en hyldeblomst.explanation: "En hyldeblomst" means "an elderflower", the small flower of the elder bush, picked in early summer. Danes make a sweet drink from it called hyldeblomstsaft (elderflower cordial).

sentence.da: En **hyldeblomst** er lille og hvid og dufter sødt.
sentence.en: An elderflower is small and white and smells sweet.

en hypotese.explanation: "En hypotese" means "a hypothesis", a guess that has not been checked yet. It is weaker than en teori (a theory), which is already supported by a lot of evidence.

sentence.da: Vi tester vores **hypotese** med et lille forsøg.
sentence.en: We test our hypothesis with a small experiment.

en hytte.explanation: "En hytte" means "a cabin" or "a hut": a small, simple house, often in the woods or the mountains. A larger holiday home is et sommerhus (a summer house).

sentence.da: Vi bor i en lille **hytte** i skoven.
sentence.en: We live in a small cabin in the forest.

en hånd.explanation: "En hånd" means "a hand". To shake hands, Danes say at give hånd (literally to give hand).

sentence.da: Jeg har fem fingre på hver **hånd**.
sentence.en: I have five fingers on each hand.

en håndbevægelse.explanation: "En håndbevægelse" means "a hand gesture", a movement of the hand that says something without words, like a wave or a thumbs-up.

sentence.da: Med en **håndbevægelse** bad han os om at være stille.
sentence.en: With a hand gesture he asked us to be quiet.

en håndflade.explanation: "En håndflade" means "a palm", the flat inside of the hand. The other side is en håndryg (the back of the hand).

sentence.da: Hun læste linjerne i min **håndflade**.
sentence.en: She read the lines in my palm.

en håndfuld.explanation: "En håndfuld" means "a handful", as much as fits in one hand: en håndfuld nødder (a handful of nuts). It also means a small number: Der var kun en håndfuld mennesker (Only a handful of people were there).

sentence.da: Hun tog en **håndfuld** mandler fra skålen.
sentence.en: She took a handful of almonds from the bowl.

en håndtaske.explanation: "En håndtaske" means "a handbag", a small bag for your phone, keys and wallet that you carry by hand or on your shoulder. It is built from hånd (hand) and taske (bag).

sentence.da: Hun har sin telefon og pung i sin **håndtaske**.
sentence.en: She has her phone and wallet in her handbag.

en håndvask.explanation: "En håndvask" means "a sink", the small basin in a bathroom. It is built from hånd (hand) and vask (wash). Håndvask also means the act of washing your hands: Husk håndvask! (Remember to wash your hands!)

sentence.da: Der er en **håndvask** ved siden af toilettet.
sentence.en: There is a sink next to the toilet.

en håndvægt.explanation: "En håndvægt" means "a dumbbell", a small weight you lift with one hand. It is built from hånd (hand) and vægt (weight). Vægt also means a scale: Jeg står på vægten (I am standing on the scale).

sentence.da: Man træner armene med en **håndvægt**.
sentence.en: You train your arms with a dumbbell.

en håndværker.explanation: "En håndværker" means "a tradesperson", someone who builds or repairs things with their hands.

sentence.da: Vi skal have en **håndværker** til at lave taget.
sentence.en: We need a tradesperson to fix the roof.

en hårbørste.explanation: "En hårbørste" means "a hairbrush". It is built from hår (hair) and børste (brush). Børste is also a verb: Jeg børster mit hår hver morgen (I brush my hair every morning).

sentence.da: En **hårbørste** er til håret, og en tandbørste er til tænderne.
sentence.en: A hairbrush is for the hair, and a toothbrush is for the teeth.

en hårelastik.explanation: "En hårelastik" means "a hair tie", a stretchy band for a ponytail. To tie your hair up, say Jeg binder håret op (I tie my hair up).

sentence.da: Jeg samler håret med en **hårelastik**.
sentence.en: I tie my hair back with a hair tie.

en hårfarve.explanation: "En hårfarve" means "a hair color", built from hår (hair) and farve (color). It is also the dye you buy: Hun har købt en ny hårfarve (She has bought a new hair dye).

sentence.da: Min **hårfarve** er brun, men min søsters er blond.
sentence.en: My hair color is brown, but my sister's is blond.

en hæftemaskine.explanation: "En hæftemaskine" means "a stapler", the office tool that presses a metal staple through paper. A staple is en hæfteklamme, and at hæfte is the verb for stapling.

sentence.da: Jeg bruger en **hæftemaskine** til at sætte papirerne sammen.
sentence.en: I use a stapler to put the papers together.

en hæk.explanation: "En hæk" means "a hedge", a tall row of plants that marks the edge of a property.

sentence.da: Vores nabo har en høj **hæk** rundt om haven.
sentence.en: Our neighbor has a tall hedge around the garden.

en hæl.explanation: "En hæl" means "a heel", the back part of your foot, and also the raised back part of a shoe. Sko med høje hæle means "shoes with high heels".

sentence.da: Min **hæl** er bag på foden.
sentence.en: My heel is at the back of the foot.

en hændelse.explanation: "En hændelse" means "an incident", something that happens, often unexpected or unwelcome. It is the word used in reports and news, for example when a workplace writes down what went wrong.

sentence.da: Politiet skriver en rapport om den **hændelse**, der skete i går.
sentence.en: The police write a report about the incident that happened yesterday.

en hængekøje.explanation: "En hængekøje" means "a hammock", a bed of cloth or net that hangs between two trees or posts. A køje (bunk) is a fixed sleeping place on a ship or in a bunk bed, and a hængekøje is one that hangs.

sentence.da: Vi hænger en **hængekøje** op mellem to træer i haven.
sentence.en: We hang a hammock between two trees in the garden.

en hær.explanation: "En hær" means "an army", a country's land forces: Han er i hæren (He is in the army). The sea and the air have their own forces, with other names.

sentence.da: Landets **hær** består af soldater og officerer.
sentence.en: The country's army consists of soldiers and officers.

en hættetrøje.explanation: "En hættetrøje" means "a hoodie", a sweater with a hood. It is built from hætte (hood) and trøje (sweater). Trøje also names a team shirt, such as en fodboldtrøje (a soccer jersey).

sentence.da: Det er koldt, og jeg tager min **hættetrøje** på.
sentence.en: It is cold, and I am putting on my hoodie.

en hæveautomat.explanation: "En hæveautomat" means "an ATM", a machine in the wall of a bank or shop where you take out cash with your card. It is built from at hæve (to withdraw) and en automat (a machine).

sentence.da: Jeg skal bruge penge fra en **hæveautomat**.
sentence.en: I need money from an ATM.

en højde.explanation: "En højde" means "a height", how far up a person or a thing reaches, such as a building or a mountain.

sentence.da: Bjerget har en **højde** på tusind meter.
sentence.en: The mountain has a height of a thousand meters.

en højhed.explanation: "En højhed" means "a highness", a title for senior members of a royal family. You use it with Hendes or Hans Kongelige Højhed (Her or His Royal Highness) when you speak about or to them formally.

sentence.da: Ordet **højhed** bruges som titel for medlemmer af kongehuset.
sentence.en: The word highness is used as a title for members of the royal family.

en højskole.explanation: "En højskole" means "a folk high school", a Danish boarding school for adults with no exams, where people live together and take courses in subjects like music, art or politics. Do not mix it up with a university: despite the name, you go to learn and meet people, not to earn a degree.

sentence.da: Hun bor på en **højskole** og synger i kor hver dag.
sentence.en: She lives at a folk high school and sings in a choir every day.

en højtid.explanation: "En højtid" means "a holiday (religious or major)", a big festive time with its own customs, such as jul (Christmas), påske (Easter) and pinse (Whitsun). It is more serious and festive than an ordinary free day.

sentence.da: Jul er den **højtid**, hvor familien samles.
sentence.en: Christmas is the holiday when the family gathers.

en højttaler.explanation: "En højttaler" means "a speaker", the device that plays sound. For a person who gives a speech, use en taler (a speaker): Taleren var god (The speaker was good).

sentence.da: Musikken kommer fra min nye **højttaler**.
sentence.en: The music comes from my new speaker.

en høne.explanation: "En høne" means "a hen", a female farm bird that lays eggs. Hens as a group are called høns.

sentence.da: En **høne** bor i hønsehuset sammen med hanen.
sentence.en: A hen lives in the chicken coop with the rooster.

en hønsegård.explanation: "En hønsegård" means "a chicken yard", the fenced place where chickens walk around outside. It is built from høns (chickens) and gård (yard). Gård also means a farm: Vi bor på en gård (We live on a farm).

sentence.da: Hønsene løber rundt i vores store **hønsegård**.
sentence.en: The chickens run around in our big chicken yard.
