en høring.explanation: "En høring" means "a hearing", a meeting where people give their views before a decision is made. It is used for public hearings in politics and also for questioning witnesses. A new law is often sent i høring (out for comment) so that groups can respond first.

sentence.da: Kommunen holder en **høring**, før den bygger den nye vej.
sentence.en: The municipality holds a hearing before it builds the new road.

en høst.explanation: "En høst" means "a harvest", the gathering of ripe crops or the amount that was gathered. The matching verb is at høste (to harvest): Vi høster æbler i september (We harvest apples in September).

sentence.da: Bønderne er glade, når årets **høst** er stor og god.
sentence.en: The farmers are happy when this year's harvest is big and good.

en høvding.explanation: "En høvding" means "a chieftain", the head of a group of related families, especially in old times or in other cultures. You mostly meet it in history books and stories about Viking times.

sentence.da: Stammens **høvding** er den, der leder og beskytter sit folk.
sentence.en: The tribe's chieftain is the one who leads and protects his people.

et halvår.explanation: "Et halvår" means "a half year", a stretch of six months, or one half of the calendar year: første halvår (the first half of the year).

sentence.da: Vi har boet i Danmark i et **halvår**, altså seks måneder.
sentence.en: We have lived in Denmark for half a year, that is, six months.

et handicap.explanation: "Et handicap" means "a disability", a long-lasting physical or mental condition that makes some things in daily life harder. For a person, you can also say Han er handicappet (He is disabled).

sentence.da: Rampen gør det nemmere for mennesker med et **handicap** at komme ind.
sentence.en: The ramp makes it easier for people with a disability to get in.

et hashtag.explanation: "Et hashtag" means "a hashtag", a word with # in front that helps people find what you share online.

sentence.da: Jeg satte et **hashtag** under mit billede.
sentence.en: I put a hashtag under my picture.

et hav.explanation: "Et hav" means "a sea" or "an ocean", a very large area of salt water. Ved havet means "by the sea", and "ud på havet" means "out at sea".

sentence.da: Skibet sejler over det store **hav**.
sentence.en: The ship sails across the big sea.

et havnebad.explanation: "Et havnebad" means "a harbor bath (outdoor pool)", a swimming area built into the water of a city harbor, open to everyone. The best known is Islands Brygge in Copenhagen, and many Danish towns now have one.

sentence.da: Om sommeren hopper børnene i vandet fra et **havnebad** midt i byen.
sentence.en: In the summer, the children jump into the water from a harbor bath in the middle of town.

et headset.explanation: "Et headset" means "a headset", something you wear on your head that lets you both listen and talk, for example in video meetings.

sentence.da: Jeg bruger mit **headset** til videomøder.
sentence.en: I use my headset for video meetings.

et hegn.explanation: "Et hegn" means "a fence", around a garden or a field. A hedge of bushes is en hæk (a hedge).

sentence.da: Hunden kan ikke komme over det høje **hegn**.
sentence.en: The dog cannot get over the tall fence.

et hensyn.explanation: "Et hensyn" means "a consideration", something you take into account, often out of care for others. It is mostly used in the phrase at tage hensyn til (to take into account): Hun tager altid hensyn til børnene (She always considers the children).

sentence.da: Af **hensyn** til naboerne slukker vi musikken klokken ti.
sentence.en: Out of consideration for the neighbors, we turn the music off at ten.

et hindbær.explanation: "Et hindbær" means "a raspberry". The second part is bær (berry), which ends many berry names: et tranebær (a cranberry), et stikkelsbær (a gooseberry).

sentence.da: Jeg laver rød marmelade af **hindbær**.
sentence.en: I make red jam from raspberries.

et hit.explanation: "Et hit" means "a hit", a movie, product or piece of music that many people like. For hitting something with your hand, use at slå (to hit).

sentence.da: Den nye sang er et stort **hit** i Danmark.
sentence.en: The new song is a big hit in Denmark.

et hjem.explanation: "Et hjem" means "a home", the place where you live and feel at home, not just the building (that is et hus, a house). Hjemme means "at home", and "hjem" alone means "toward home": Jeg går hjem means "I am going home".

sentence.da: Min familie er mit **hjem**.
sentence.en: My family is my home.

et hjemland.explanation: "Et hjemland" means "a home country", the country you come from or belong to, often used by people who live abroad: Mange savner deres hjemland (Many people miss their home country).

sentence.da: Det land, man kommer fra, kaldes ens **hjemland**.
sentence.en: The country you come from is called your home country.

et hjerte.explanation: "Et hjerte" means "a heart". The h is silent, so the word starts like the y in the English word yes. It is also used for feelings, as in med hele mit hjerte (with all my heart).

sentence.da: Mit **hjerte** slår hurtigt.
sentence.en: My heart is beating fast.

et hjerteanfald.explanation: "Et hjerteanfald" means "a heart attack", a sudden emergency when part of the heart muscle is cut off from its blood supply. In Denmark, you call 112 right away. It is not the same as et hjertestop (cardiac arrest), where the heart stops beating.

sentence.da: Han fik et **hjerteanfald**, men ambulancen kom hurtigt og reddede ham.
sentence.en: He had a heart attack, but the ambulance came quickly and saved him.

et hjerteslag.explanation: "Et hjerteslag" means "a heartbeat", one single beat of the heart. How many you have in a minute is called puls (pulse).

sentence.da: Lægen lytter efter patientens **hjerteslag** med et stetoskop.
sentence.en: The doctor listens for the patient's heartbeat with a stethoscope.

et hjertestop.explanation: "Et hjertestop" means "a cardiac arrest", the moment the heart suddenly stops pumping blood. The person collapses and needs help at once, because the brain gets no more oxygen. It is not the same as et hjerteanfald (a heart attack).

sentence.da: Ved **hjertestop** skal man straks ringe 112 og starte hjertemassage.
sentence.en: In a cardiac arrest, you must call 112 at once and start chest compressions.

et hjul.explanation: "Et hjul" means "a wheel", on a car, a bike or a cart.

sentence.da: Jeg skal skifte et **hjul** på bilen.
sentence.en: I have to change a wheel on the car.

et hjørne.explanation: "Et hjørne" means "a corner" of a room, a street or a shape: Stolen står i hjørnet (The chair is in the corner). Butikken ligger på hjørnet (The store is on the corner).

sentence.da: Der er en lampe i hvert **hjørne** af rummet.
sentence.en: There is a lamp in every corner of the room.

et hjørnespark.explanation: "Et hjørnespark" means "a corner kick", a kick in soccer taken from the corner of the field. The attacking team gets it when the other team kicks the ball out over its own end line.

sentence.da: Spilleren stiller bolden ved flaget og tager et **hjørnespark**.
sentence.en: The player puts the ball by the flag and takes a corner kick.

et hobbyrum.explanation: "Et hobbyrum" means "a hobby room", a room at home for crafts and other hobbies.

sentence.da: Min mand bygger modelskibe i et lille **hobbyrum**.
sentence.en: My husband builds model ships in a small hobby room.

et hold.explanation: "Et hold" means "a team", people playing or working together: Vi er et godt hold (We are a good team). It also means a course you sign up for: Jeg går på et hold om aftenen (I take a course in the evening).

sentence.da: Vores **hold** vandt kampen i går.
sentence.en: Our team won the match yesterday.

et horn.explanation: "Et horn" means "a horn", the hard, pointed growth on the head of a cow or a ram. It is also a musical instrument you blow into: et jagthorn (a hunting horn). A deer does not have horns but et gevir (antlers), which fall off and grow back each year.

sentence.da: Både tyre og køer har **horn** på hovedet.
sentence.en: Both bulls and cows have horns on their heads.

et hospital.explanation: "Et hospital" means "a hospital". På hospitalet means "at the hospital". Danes also say et sygehus (literally a sick house) for a hospital.

sentence.da: Lægen arbejder på et **hospital**.
sentence.en: The doctor works at a hospital.

et hotel.explanation: "Et hotel" means "a hotel". På hotellet means "at the hotel". To say you are staying at one, Danes say Vi bor på hotel (We are staying at a hotel).

sentence.da: På et **hotel** kan man sove.
sentence.en: At a hotel you can sleep.

et hotelværelse.explanation: "Et hotelværelse" means "a hotel room". It is made of et hotel (a hotel) and et værelse (a room). Værelse alone can mean any room you sleep in or rent.

sentence.da: Mit **hotelværelse** har udsigt til havnen.
sentence.en: My hotel room has a view of the harbor.

et hoved.explanation: "Et hoved" means "a head". For aches, Danish says the head where English says my head: Jeg har ondt i hovedet is literally I have a pain in the head, and means "my head hurts". It is also part of hovedpine (headache) and hovedstad (capital city).

sentence.da: Hun har en stor hat på sit **hoved**.
sentence.en: She has a big hat on her head.

et hovedkvarter.explanation: "Et hovedkvarter" means "a headquarters", the main base that a company, an organization or an army is run from. The other places it has are smaller and report to it.

sentence.da: Firmaets **hovedkvarter** ligger i København, men der er kontorer i hele landet.
sentence.en: The company's headquarters is in Copenhagen, but there are offices all over the country.

et hul.explanation: "Et hul" means "a hole", in the ground, in a wall or in clothes. It can also be a weak spot or something missing: et hul i budgettet (a hole in the budget).

sentence.da: Hunden graver et **hul** i haven.
sentence.en: The dog is digging a hole in the garden.

et humør.explanation: "Et humør" means "a mood", how a person feels right now: Han er i dårligt humør (He is in a bad mood).

sentence.da: Hun er i godt **humør** i dag.
sentence.en: She is in a good mood today.

et hundehalsbånd.explanation: "Et hundehalsbånd" means "a dog collar", a band around a dog's neck, often with the owner's phone number on it. It is built from hund (dog), hals (neck) and bånd (band).

sentence.da: Hunden har et nyt **hundehalsbånd** på.
sentence.en: The dog has a new dog collar on.

et hus.explanation: "Et hus" means "a house", the building where people live. Do not mix it up with et hjem (a home), which is about the place where you feel at home rather than the building.

sentence.da: Et **hus** har vægge, et tag og vinduer.
sentence.en: A house has walls, a roof and windows.

et husdyr.explanation: "Et husdyr" means "a domestic animal" or "a pet", built from hus (house) and dyr (animal). It also covers animals kept for food or work, like a cow or a hen, and not only animals kept for company.

sentence.da: Vi har to **husdyr**: en kat og en hund.
sentence.en: We have two pets: a cat and a dog.

et husnummer.explanation: "Et husnummer" means "a house number", the number that marks one building. It comes after the name, not before it: Nørregade 12 (12 is the house number).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke se dit **husnummer** på døren.
sentence.en: I cannot see your house number on the door.

et håndarbejde.explanation: "Et håndarbejde" means "a handicraft", work made by hand with thread, yarn or cloth. Do not mix it up with et håndværk (a trade like carpentry). Hun sidder og laver håndarbejde (She sits and does needlework).

sentence.da: Strikning og broderi er begge slags **håndarbejde**.
sentence.en: Knitting and embroidery are both kinds of handicraft.

et håndjern.explanation: "Et håndjern" means "a handcuff", a metal ring that locks around a wrist. Because they come as a pair, you almost always see håndjern in the plural. To be handcuffed is at være i håndjern.

sentence.da: Politiet anholdt manden og tog **håndjern** på ham.
sentence.en: The police arrested the man and put handcuffs on him.

et håndklæde.explanation: "Et håndklæde" means "a towel" for drying your body or hands. A towel for dishes is et viskestykke (a dish towel).

sentence.da: Efter badet tørrer jeg mig med et **håndklæde**.
sentence.en: After the bath, I dry myself with a towel.

et håndled.explanation: "Et håndled" means "a wrist", the joint between your hand and your arm. It is built from en hånd (a hand) and et led (a joint). Et led also means a link: et led i en kæde (a link in a chain).

sentence.da: Han har et ur om sit **håndled**.
sentence.en: He has a watch around his wrist.

et håndtag.explanation: "Et håndtag" means "a handle", for example on a drawer or a bag. It is built from en hånd (a hand) and et tag (a hold), so it is what you take hold of.

sentence.da: Skuffen går ikke op, fordi dens **håndtag** er gået i stykker.
sentence.en: The drawer will not open, because its handle is broken.

et håndtryk.explanation: "Et håndtryk" means "a handshake", the usual way of saying hello to someone you meet for the first time. The action is at give hånd (to shake hands).

sentence.da: Aftalen blev sluttet med et fast **håndtryk**.
sentence.en: The deal was sealed with a firm handshake.

et håndværk.explanation: "Et håndværk" means "a craft", a skilled trade done with the hands and tools, such as building houses or repairing pipes. You usually train for it as a young person in a training program with a workplace.

sentence.da: Det tager flere år at lære et **håndværk**, for eksempel som tømrer.
sentence.en: It takes several years to learn a craft, for example as a carpenter.

et hårspænde.explanation: "Et hårspænde" means "a hair clip", a small clip that holds hair in place. It is built from hår (hair) and et spænde (a clasp). Spænde also means a buckle: et bæltespænde (a belt buckle).

sentence.da: Hun har et lille **hårspænde** i håret.
sentence.en: She has a small hair clip in her hair.

et hæfte.explanation: "Et hæfte" means "a notebook", a thin one with a soft cover for school work. It can also be a thin booklet that comes with something: et hæfte med opskrifter (a booklet of recipes).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver mine lektier i mit **hæfte**.
sentence.en: I write my homework in my notebook.

et højhus.explanation: "Et højhus" means "a high-rise", a tall building with many levels. It is built from høj (tall) and hus (house). Høj also means loud: Musikken er for høj (The music is too loud).

sentence.da: Hun bor meget højt oppe i et **højhus**.
sentence.en: She lives very high up in a high-rise.

et højskoleophold.explanation: "Et højskoleophold" means "a folk high school stay", a stay of a few weeks or months at a højskole, a school for adults. There are no exams, and you choose subjects like music, art or politics.

sentence.da: På et **højskoleophold** bor man på skolen og lærer noget sammen med andre.
sentence.en: On a folk high school stay, you live at the school and learn something together with others.

et høreapparat.explanation: "Et høreapparat" means "a hearing aid", a small device worn in or behind the ear that makes sounds louder. People who have trouble hearing get it from a specialist.

sentence.da: Min bedstefar har fået et **høreapparat**, så han kan høre fjernsynet.
sentence.en: My grandfather has gotten a hearing aid, so he can hear the TV.

had.explanation: "Had" means "hatred", a very strong dislike. Use mod for who or what is hated: Hun følte had mod ham (She felt hatred toward him).

sentence.da: Der var **had** i hans stemme.
sentence.en: There was hatred in his voice.

hagl.explanation: "Hagl" means "hail", hard lumps of ice that fall from the sky, often during a storm. It is also the word for the small pellets in a shotgun: a haglgevær (shotgun) shoots hagl.

sentence.da: Store **hagl** faldt og ødelagde ruden på bilen.
sentence.en: Large hail fell and broke the window of the car.

hakket oksekød.explanation: "Hakket oksekød" means "ground beef". It is built from hakket (chopped) and oksekød (beef), so it is beef cut into tiny pieces. For pork, say hakket svinekød (ground pork).

sentence.da: Vi bruger **hakket oksekød** til lasagne.
sentence.en: We use ground beef for lasagna.

hallo.explanation: "Hallo" means "hello". Danes use it when answering the phone and when calling out to get someone's attention. For greeting someone face to face, they prefer hej (hi). Said sharply, it means "hey, listen!": Hallo, hører du efter? (Hey, are you listening?).

sentence.da: Telefonen ringer. **Hallo**, hvem er det?
sentence.en: The phone rings. Hello, who is it?

halløj.explanation: "Halløj" means "hey" or "hello there" and is a cheerful, playful greeting. It suits friends and family, but is too playful for a job interview.

sentence.da: **Halløj**, har I det godt?
sentence.en: Hey, are you all doing well?

halm.explanation: "Halm" means "straw", the dry stalks left in the field after grain such as wheat is harvested. It is not a drinking straw, which is et sugerør. Farmers use halm as bedding for animals, while hø (hay) is food for them.

sentence.da: Taget på det gamle hus er lavet af **halm**.
sentence.en: The roof of the old house is made of straw.

halv.explanation: "Halv" means "half" and goes before the thing it measures. On the clock, it counts toward the next hour: klokken fire is 4:00, but halv fire is 3:30, half an hour before four, not after three.

sentence.da: En **halv** time er tredive minutter.
sentence.en: Half an hour is thirty minutes.

halv tre.explanation: "Halv tre" means "half past two", not half past three. Danes count halfway toward the next hour, so 2:30 is halv tre (halfway to three).

forms.en: See you at half past six.

sentence.da: Det er **halv tre**, tredive minutter før tre.
sentence.en: It is half past two, thirty minutes before three.

halvanden.explanation: "Halvanden" means "one and a half". It goes before en-words: halvanden meter (one and a half meters). Before et-words, use halvandet: halvandet kilo (one and a half kilos).

sentence.da: Jeg venter i **halvanden** time.
sentence.en: I am waiting for an hour and a half.

halvdelen.explanation: "Halvdelen" means "the half (of it)". You usually say what it is half of with af (of). To say just half a (something), use halv (half), as in en halv liter (half a liter).

sentence.da: Jeg har spist **halvdelen** af kagen.
sentence.en: I have eaten half of the cake.

halvfems.explanation: "Halvfems" means "ninety". It is short for halvfemsindstyve: halfway to five twenties (4½ x 20 = 90). For 91, you say enoghalvfems (literally one-and-ninety).

sentence.da: Min bedstefar er **halvfems** år og snart hundrede.
sentence.en: My grandfather is ninety years old and will soon be a hundred.

halvfjerds.explanation: "Halvfjerds" means "seventy". Danes count it as halfway to four twenties (3½ x 20 = 70). For 71, you say enoghalvfjerds (literally one-and-seventy). Do not mix it up with halvfems (ninety).

sentence.da: **Halvfjerds** er ti mere end tres.
sentence.en: Seventy is ten more than sixty.

halvtreds.explanation: "Halvtreds" means "fifty". Danes count it as halfway to three twenties (2½ x 20 = 50). For 51, you say enoghalvtreds (literally one-and-fifty).

sentence.da: **Halvtreds** er det halve af hundrede.
sentence.en: Fifty is half of a hundred.

halvvejs.explanation: "Halvvejs" means "halfway", at the point where half of a distance or a task is done. It is built from halv (half) and vej (way). It also works for time: halvvejs gennem året (halfway through the year).

sentence.da: Vi har kørt i to timer og er nu **halvvejs**.
sentence.en: We have driven for two hours and are now halfway.

ham.explanation: "Ham" means "him". Compare Han hjælper mig (He helps me) with Jeg hjælper ham (I help him): han is the man who helps, ham is the man who gets the help. Ham is also used after words like til (to) and med (with): til ham, med ham (to him, with him). Hans is a different word, meaning "his".

sentence.da: Peter er min ven. Jeg kan lide **ham**.
sentence.en: Peter is my friend. I like him.

han.explanation: "Han" means "he". Compare Han hjælper mig (He helps me) with Jeg hjælper ham (I help him): han is the man who helps, ham is the man who gets the help. Hans means "his": hans bil (his car).

sentence.da: **Han** er min bror.
sentence.en: He is my brother.

handsker.explanation: "Handsker" means "gloves", built from hånd (hand). Gloves have separate fingers. Mittens do not, and they are called vanter.

sentence.da: Om vinteren har jeg **handsker** på hænderne.
sentence.en: In winter I wear gloves on my hands.

hans.explanation: "Hans" means "his" and never changes, whatever word follows. Compare Peter vasker hans bil (Peter washes some other man's car) with Peter vasker sin bil (Peter washes his own car).

sentence.da: Peter har en hund. **Hans** hund er stor.
sentence.en: Peter has a dog. His dog is big.

hardware.explanation: "Hardware" means "hardware", the parts of a computer you can touch.

sentence.da: Min computer er gammel, så jeg køber ny **hardware**.
sentence.en: My computer is old, so I am buying new hardware.

hav en god dag.explanation: "Hav en god dag" means "have a good day" and is a friendly goodbye in shops and offices. You can swap dag (day) for aften (evening) or "weekend". The usual reply is i lige måde (same to you).

sentence.da: Tak for hjælpen. **Hav en god dag**!
sentence.en: Thanks for the help. Have a good day!

havearbejde.explanation: "Havearbejde" means "gardening", the work you do in a garden. It is built from have (garden) and arbejde (work). Arbejde is also where you work: Jeg er på arbejde (I am at work).

sentence.da: **Havearbejde** er at plante blomster og klippe græs.
sentence.en: Gardening is planting flowers and cutting grass.

havre.explanation: "Havre" means "oats", the plant that porridge is made from. For breakfast, Danes eat havregryn (rolled oats) or havregrød (oatmeal).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser grød med **havre** hver morgen.
sentence.en: I eat porridge with oats every morning.

havregryn.explanation: "Havregryn" means "rolled oats" or "oatmeal", the dry flakes you cook or soak. Cooked into porridge, it is called havregrød (oatmeal porridge).

forms.en: We have oatmeal in the cupboard.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser **havregryn** med mælk og banan.
sentence.en: I eat oatmeal with milk and banana.

havremælk.explanation: "Havremælk" means "oat milk", a plant drink people use instead of cow's milk. It is havre (oats) and mælk (milk) joined together.

sentence.da: **Havremælk** er en drik lavet af havre.
sentence.en: Oat milk is a drink made from oats.

hed.explanation: "Hed" means "hot" and is used for strong heat, hotter than varm (warm).

sentence.da: Kaffen er så **hed**, at jeg brænder tungen.
sentence.en: The coffee is so hot that I burn my tongue.

hej.explanation: "Hej" means "hi" or "hello" and is used with almost everyone, friends and strangers, young and old. It is also used when you leave, often as hej hej (bye bye).

sentence.da: **Hej**, jeg hedder Anna.
sentence.en: Hi, my name is Anna.

hej med dig.explanation: "Hej med dig" means "hi there" when you meet and "bye" when you part, so the meaning depends on the moment. For several people, say hej med jer (hi to you all). Hej hej (said twice) is mostly used for goodbye.

sentence.da: **Hej med dig**, Anna!
sentence.en: Hi there, Anna!

hejsa.explanation: "Hejsa" means "hi there" or "hey". It is a cheerful, informal version of hej (hi). Use it with friends, family and children. In formal situations, goddag (good day) is better.

sentence.da: **Hejsa**, Peter!
sentence.en: Hi there, Peter!

hektisk.explanation: "Hektisk" means "hectic", full of things to do and moving fast. It usually describes a time or a place rather than a person.

sentence.da: Det var en **hektisk** dag med møder fra morgen til aften.
sentence.en: It was a hectic day with meetings from morning to evening.

hel.explanation: "Hel" means "whole" or "entire": en hel kage (a whole cake). When you mean "the whole ...", use hele: hele dagen (the whole day). It also means "unbroken": Koppen er hel (The cup is unbroken).

sentence.da: Jeg spiste en **hel** pizza og ikke bare et stykke.
sentence.en: I ate a whole pizza and not just a slice.

helbred.explanation: "Helbred" means "health". It is about how well your body is doing. For food that is good for you, use sund (healthy): sund mad (healthy food).

sentence.da: Min bedstefar har et godt **helbred**.
sentence.en: My grandfather has good health.

held.explanation: "Held" means "luck", or good fortune in a situation: Vi havde held med vejret (We were lucky with the weather).

sentence.da: Jeg havde **held** og fandt en ledig plads.
sentence.en: I had luck and found a free seat.

held og lykke.explanation: "Held og lykke" means "good luck". Literally, it is luck and happiness. Add med (with) and what it is about: held og lykke med prøven (good luck with the test).

sentence.da: **Held og lykke** med dit nye job!
sentence.en: Good luck with your new job!

heldig.explanation: "Heldig" means "lucky". It comes from held (luck). It also gives you heldigvis (luckily).

sentence.da: Jeg var **heldig** og vandt en bil.
sentence.en: I was lucky and won a car.

heldigvis.explanation: "Heldigvis" means "fortunately" and shows you are glad about something. The opposite is desværre (unfortunately).

sentence.da: **Heldigvis** havde jeg en paraply med.
sentence.en: Fortunately I had an umbrella with me.

hele tiden.explanation: "Hele tiden" means "all the time". It often sounds like a complaint: Telefonen ringer hele tiden (The phone rings all the time). For a neutral "always", say altid (always).

sentence.da: Hun ringer **hele tiden**.
sentence.en: She calls all the time.

heller.explanation: "Heller" means "either", as in can't ... either. Compare Jeg kan også komme (I can come too) with Jeg kan heller ikke komme (I can't come either). Heller always goes with a no-word like ikke (not): heller ikke i dag (not today either).

sentence.da: Han kommer ikke, og jeg kommer **heller** ikke.
sentence.en: He is not coming, and I am not coming either.

hellere.explanation: "Hellere" means "rather". It says what you would choose instead. With må (must) it means "had better", a strong hint to do something. Do not mix it up with heller in heller ikke (not ... either).

forms.da: hellere i dag end i morgen

sentence.da: Jeg vil **hellere** gå end tage bussen.
sentence.en: I would rather walk than take the bus.

hellere end.explanation: "Hellere end" means "rather than" and shows what you would not choose: Jeg spiser hellere ris end pasta (I would rather eat rice than pasta). Hellere alone means "rather".

sentence.da: Jeg vil blive hjemme **hellere end** at gå ud.
sentence.en: I would rather stay home than go out.

hellig.explanation: "Hellig" means "holy" or "sacred", connected to God or religion and treated with deep respect.

sentence.da: Kirken er **hellig** for de troende.
sentence.en: The church is holy to the believers.

helst.explanation: "Helst" means "preferably" or "most of all". It shows your first choice. Helst ikke is a soft no: Skal du med? - Helst ikke (Are you coming? - Preferably not).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **helst** bo ved havet.
sentence.en: I would most like to live by the sea.

helt.explanation: "Helt" means "completely". It makes the next word stronger. Compare Jeg er enig (I agree) with Jeg er helt enig (I completely agree), and næsten færdig (almost done) with helt færdig (completely done).

sentence.da: Glasset er **helt** tomt.
sentence.en: The glass is completely empty.

hemmelig.explanation: "Hemmelig" means "secret", for what others must not know. A secret itself is en hemmelighed.

sentence.da: Vi har en **hemmelig** plan til din fødselsdag.
sentence.en: We have a secret plan for your birthday.

hemmelighedsfuld.explanation: "Hemmelighedsfuld" means "secretive", for someone who tells little and acts as if there is more to hide. The ending -fuld (full of) shows up in many words for a quality, such as hensynsfuld (considerate).

sentence.da: Hun er **hemmelighedsfuld** og fortæller aldrig noget om sig selv.
sentence.en: She is secretive and never tells anything about herself.

hen.explanation: "Hen" means "over" or "toward" and shows movement to a place: Gå hen til døren (Walk over to the door). For where something already is, use henne (over there): Han står henne ved døren (He stands over there by the door).

sentence.da: Hun går **hen** til sin ven og siger hej.
sentence.en: She walks over to her friend and says hi.

hende.explanation: "Hende" means "her". Compare Hun hjælper mig (She helps me) with Jeg hjælper hende (I help her): hun is the woman who helps, hende is the woman who gets the help. It is also used after words like til (to) and med (with): til hende, med hende (to her, with her). Hendes is a different word: hendes bil (her car).

sentence.da: Anna er min ven. Jeg kan lide **hende**.
sentence.en: Anna is my friend. I like her.

hendes.explanation: "Hendes" means "her" or "hers", for something that belongs to a woman or girl: Anna har en taske. Det er hendes taske (Anna has a bag. It is her bag). It never changes, whatever word follows. Compare Anna vasker hendes bil (Anna washes some other woman's car) with Anna vasker sin bil (Anna washes her own car).

sentence.da: Bilen er **hendes**, ikke min.
sentence.en: The car is hers, not mine.

hensynsfuld.explanation: "Hensynsfuld" means "considerate", for someone who thinks about how their actions affect others, for example when sharing a room or a table. The opposite is made by adding u-: uhensynsfuld (inconsiderate).

sentence.da: Han er **hensynsfuld** og går stille forbi, når babyen sover.
sentence.en: He is considerate and walks past quietly when the baby is sleeping.

her.explanation: "Her" means "here", the place where you are. Compare Jeg står her (I am standing here) with Du står der (You are standing there). Careful: it looks like the English word her, but that word is hende in Danish. In everyday speech, den her bog means "this book".

sentence.da: Jeg bor **her** i huset.
sentence.en: I live here in the house.

herfra.explanation: "Herfra" means "from here" and tells where you start. It is built from her (here) and fra (from). For a place away from you, use derfra (from there).

forms.en: From here you can see the town

sentence.da: **Herfra** er der kun fem minutter til stationen.
sentence.en: From here it is only five minutes to the station.

herhen.explanation: "Herhen" means "(to) here" and is used when something moves toward you. To say where someone is, use her (here): Jeg er her (I am here).

sentence.da: Kan du komme **herhen** et øjeblik?
sentence.en: Can you come here for a moment?

herinde.explanation: "Herinde" means "in here". You say it when you are inside the place yourself. Someone outside says derinde (in there): Hun er derinde (She is in there). To move inside, use ind: Kom ind! (Come in!).

sentence.da: Jeg er **herinde**, ikke udenfor.
sentence.en: I am in here, not outside.

herlig.explanation: "Herlig" means "wonderful" or "lovely" and is used warmly for food, weather, days and people: Maden var herlig (The food was wonderful).

sentence.da: Solen skinner, og dagen er **herlig**.
sentence.en: The sun is shining, and the day is wonderful.

hermed.explanation: "Hermed" means "hereby" or "herewith", used when the words themselves do the action: Hermed åbner jeg mødet (I hereby open the meeting). In emails it goes with something you send along: Hermed sender jeg kontrakten (Attached is the contract).

forms.en: The meeting is hereby declared open

sentence.da: **Hermed** sender jeg dig regningen og et par billeder.
sentence.en: I hereby send you the bill and a few pictures.

hertil.explanation: "Hertil" means "to here" or "to this": Hertil kommer prisen (On top of this comes the price). It also tells where you have been: Jeg har ikke været hertil før (I have not been here before).

sentence.da: Vi tog toget **hertil** i går.
sentence.en: We took the train here yesterday.

herude.explanation: "Herude" means "out here" and tells where you are when you are outside or far out. For a place away from you, use derude (out there).

sentence.da: Jeg fryser, når jeg står **herude** uden jakke.
sentence.en: I freeze when I stand out here without a jacket.

hidsig.explanation: "Hidsig" means "hot-tempered", for someone who gets angry quickly and strongly. It describes a person's nature, not one moment of anger; for a single moment, use vred (angry).

sentence.da: Han er **hidsig** og råber af folk for små ting.
sentence.en: He is hot-tempered and shouts at people over small things.

hidtil.explanation: "Hidtil" means "so far" or "until now", looking back from now over the past. It needs no end point. For an end point, use indtil (until): indtil fredag (until Friday).

forms.en: So far it has gone well

sentence.da: **Hidtil** har jeg kun boet i Danmark.
sentence.en: So far, I have only lived in Denmark.

hinanden.explanation: "Hinanden" means "each other" and is used when people do the same thing to one another, so the action goes both ways. Compare De vasker sig (They wash themselves) with De vasker hinanden (They wash each other).

sentence.da: Min mor og far elsker **hinanden**.
sentence.en: My mom and dad love each other.

hinsides.explanation: "Hinsides" means "beyond", on the far side of a place such as a river or a border. It is also used for what is out of reach, such as something people cannot explain.

sentence.da: Vi skal over broen, fordi byen ligger **hinsides** floden.
sentence.en: We have to cross the bridge because the town lies beyond the river.

historisk.explanation: "Historisk" means "historic" and "historical". It can be about something important: en historisk dag (a historic day). It can also be about the past: en historisk roman (a historical novel).

sentence.da: Det var en **historisk** aften for hele landet.
sentence.en: It was a historic evening for the whole country.

hittegods.explanation: "Hittegods" means "lost and found", the things people have lost and others have found, and also the place where you ask for them: Hittegodset er åbent i dag (The lost and found is open today).

forms.en: I am looking for the lost and found
We hand it in as lost property
It is in the lost and found

sentence.da: Har I **hittegods**? Jeg har mistet min jakke.
sentence.en: Do you have lost property? I have lost my jacket.

hjem.explanation: "Hjem" means "home" when you are heading there. Compare Jeg går hjem (I am going home) with Jeg er hjemme (I am at home). Hjem goes with words for moving, like gå (go), køre (drive) and komme (come).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **hjem** nu.
sentence.en: I am going home now.

hjemlig.explanation: "Hjemlig" means "homey", feeling like home, cozy and familiar. It can also mean "domestic", from your own country: hjemlig produktion (domestic production).

sentence.da: Cafeen har en **hjemlig** stemning med bløde stole og levende lys.
sentence.en: The cafe has a homey atmosphere with soft chairs and candles.

hjemløs.explanation: "Hjemløs" means "homeless", without a place to live. It is built from hjem (home) and the ending -løs (without). It can also be used for the person: en hjemløs (a homeless person).

sentence.da: Manden er **hjemløs** og sover på gaden om natten.
sentence.en: The man is homeless and sleeps on the street at night.

hjemme.explanation: "Hjemme" means "at home", where you already are. Compare Jeg er hjemme (I am at home) with Jeg går hjem (I am going home).

sentence.da: Jeg er **hjemme** i aften.
sentence.en: I am at home tonight.

hjemmelavet.explanation: "Hjemmelavet" means "homemade", made at home and not in a factory. It is built from hjemme (at home) and lavet (made). Lavet is also in håndlavet (handmade).

sentence.da: Kagen er **hjemmelavet**, ikke købt i butikken.
sentence.en: The cake is homemade, not bought in the store.

hjælp.explanation: "Hjælp" means "help", used without en (a) in front: Kan jeg få hjælp? (Can I get help?)

sentence.da: Jeg har brug for **hjælp**!
sentence.en: I need help!

hjælpeløs.explanation: "Hjælpeløs" means "helpless", unable to do anything about a situation. It also describes a feeling: Jeg følte mig hjælpeløs (I felt helpless). Do not confuse it with hjælpsom (helpful).

sentence.da: En nyfødt baby er **hjælpeløs** og har brug for sine forældre.
sentence.en: A newborn baby is helpless and needs its parents.

hjælpsom.explanation: "Hjælpsom" means "helpful" and describes a person who is ready to lend a hand. It is not for a useful thing: a useful tip is et nyttigt tip.

sentence.da: Min nabo er **hjælpsom** og bærer mine poser.
sentence.en: My neighbor is helpful and carries my bags.

hjælpsomhed.explanation: "Hjælpsomhed" means "helpfulness", the habit of helping other people when they need it. It describes a person's character, so it is often used in praise: Din hjælpsomhed betyder meget (Your helpfulness means a lot).

sentence.da: Alle roser hans **hjælpsomhed**, fordi han altid hjælper sine naboer.
sentence.en: Everyone praises his helpfulness because he always helps his neighbors.

hold da op.explanation: "Hold da op" means "wow" or "whoa", said when you are impressed or surprised. It looks like hold op (stop it), but the small word da (then) turns the order into a reaction.

sentence.da: **Hold da op**, hvor er den bil hurtig!
sentence.en: Wow, that car is fast!

hold kæft.explanation: "Hold kæft" means "shut up" and is rude. Use it only as a joke with close friends, never with strangers or at work. It can also be a loud reaction of surprise, like No way! in English.

forms.da: Hold kæft, hvor er det flot!

sentence.da: **Hold kæft**, jeg troede ikke, du ville komme!
sentence.en: Wow, I did not think you would come!

hold op.explanation: "Hold op" means "stop it" or "stop". Use med at (with) before the thing you stop doing: Jeg holder op med at ryge (I am quitting smoking).

sentence.da: **Hold op** med at drille mig!
sentence.en: Stop teasing me!

holdbar.explanation: "Holdbar" means "durable", able to last without breaking or going bad. For food, it tells how long it keeps, and the date is called en holdbarhedsdato (a best-before date). It can also describe an idea that stands up to questions: en holdbar forklaring (a tenable explanation).

sentence.da: Cyklen er **holdbar** og kan klare mange års brug.
sentence.en: The bike is durable and can handle many years of use.

holland.explanation: "Holland" means "the Netherlands", with no word for the in front: Jeg bor i Holland (I live in the Netherlands). Danes use it for the whole country; the formal name Nederlandene (the Netherlands) is rarely heard.

sentence.da: I **Holland** taler de hollandsk.
sentence.en: In the Netherlands they speak Dutch.

hollandsk.explanation: "Hollandsk" means "Dutch", both for things from the Netherlands and for the language. Danish writes it with a lowercase first letter, even though Dutch has a capital D in English.

sentence.da: Han bor i Holland og taler **hollandsk**.
sentence.en: He lives in the Netherlands and speaks Dutch.

honning.explanation: "Honning" means "honey", the sweet, sticky food that bees make.

sentence.da: Bier laver **honning** af blomster.
sentence.en: Bees make honey from flowers.

hos.explanation: "Hos" means "at someone's place", and a person comes after it: hos min ven (at my friend's place), hos lægen (at the doctor's). For a building or place, use på (at) or i (in): på biblioteket (at the library), i køkkenet (in the kitchen). Compare Jeg er hos lægen (I am at the doctor's) with Jeg er på hospitalet (I am at the hospital).

sentence.da: Jeg sover **hos** min ven i nat.
sentence.en: I am sleeping at my friend's place tonight.

hovedsagelig.explanation: "Hovedsagelig" means "mainly", for the biggest part but not all of it. It is built from hovedsag (the main matter), so it points to the core of something. The form hovedsageligt means the same.

sentence.da: Jeg læser **hovedsagelig** krimier, men nogle gange også biografier.
sentence.en: I mainly read crime novels, but sometimes also biographies.

hovedsageligt.explanation: "Hovedsageligt" means "mainly", and it is the same as hovedsagelig, so both are correct. It often introduces the main reason: hovedsageligt på grund af vejret (mainly because of the weather).

sentence.da: Flyet var **hovedsageligt** fyldt med turister, men også nogle forretningsfolk.
sentence.en: The plane was mainly full of tourists, but also some business people.

hud.explanation: "En hud" means "a skin", but Danes mostly just say hud for the skin on your body. You will also see it in hudcreme (skin cream).

sentence.da: Solen kan brænde din **hud**.
sentence.en: The sun can burn your skin.

humor.explanation: "Humor" means "humor", what makes things funny. To say someone has a sense of humor, use sans (sense) with for: Hun har sans for humor (She has a sense of humor).

sentence.da: Hun fortæller vittigheder og har god **humor**.
sentence.en: She tells jokes and has a good sense of humor.

humoristisk.explanation: "Humoristisk" means "humorous", meant to make people smile or laugh. It describes a style or a piece of work, such as a talk or a book. In everyday talk, Danes say sjov (funny): Det var sjovt! (That was fun!)

sentence.da: Hans tale var **humoristisk**, og hele salen grinede.
sentence.en: His speech was humorous, and the whole room laughed.

hun.explanation: "Hun" means "she". Compare Hun hjælper mig (She helps me) with Jeg hjælper hende (I help her): hun is the woman who helps, hende is the woman who gets the help.

sentence.da: **Hun** er min søster.
sentence.en: She is my sister.

hundemad.explanation: "Hundemad" means "dog food". It is built from hund (dog) and mad (food), and mad also builds morgenmad (breakfast) and aftensmad (dinner).

sentence.da: Hunden får **hundemad** to gange om dagen.
sentence.en: The dog gets dog food twice a day.

hundrede.explanation: "Hundrede" means "hundred". It stays the same after other numbers: to hundrede (200) and tre hundrede (300). For 100, you can just say hundrede, with no one in front.

sentence.da: Ti gange ti er **hundrede**.
sentence.en: Ten times ten is a hundred.

hundrededel.explanation: "En hundrededel" means "a hundredth", one of a hundred equal parts. It is built from hundrede (hundred) and del (part). The same pattern gives other fractions: en tiendedel (a tenth).

sentence.da: Han vandt løbet med kun en **hundrededel** af et sekund.
sentence.en: He won the race by only a hundredth of a second.

hurra.explanation: "Hurra" means "hooray" and is a cheer for good news or a win. Add for and a person to cheer for them: Hurra for fødselaren! (Hooray for the birthday person!).

sentence.da: **Hurra**, vi har fri i dag!
sentence.en: Hooray, we have the day off today!

hurtig.explanation: "Hurtig" means "fast" or "quick", for people, cars, answers and actions. To say how someone does something, use hurtigt (quickly): Han løber hurtigt (He runs fast).

sentence.da: Racerbilen er meget **hurtig**.
sentence.en: The race car is very fast.

husarbejde.explanation: "Husarbejde" means "housework", the jobs you do to keep a home in order. Arbejde (work) also means a job: Jeg har et nyt arbejde (I have a new job).

sentence.da: Jeg hader **husarbejde**, men jeg gør rent hver lørdag.
sentence.en: I hate housework, but I clean every Saturday.

husholdningsfilm.explanation: "Husholdningsfilm" means "plastic wrap", thin transparent plastic that you wrap around food or a bowl to keep it fresh. It is built from husholdning (household) and film, which here means a thin sheet and not a movie.

sentence.da: Jeg dækker skålen med **husholdningsfilm** og sætter den i køleskabet.
sentence.en: I cover the bowl with plastic wrap and put it in the refrigerator.

husleje.explanation: "Husleje" means "rent", the money you pay each month to live in a home. Leje (rental) also works as a verb: at leje en bil (to rent a car).

sentence.da: Jeg betaler **husleje** den første hver måned.
sentence.en: I pay rent on the first of every month.

hvabehar.explanation: "Hvabehar" means "pardon?" and asks someone to say it again. It is one word spoken fast, from hvad behager (what pleases). Said sharply, it can also show surprise, like What! in English.

sentence.da: **Hvabehar**? Kan du sige det igen?
sentence.en: Pardon? Can you say it again?

hvad.explanation: "Hvad" means "what" and asks about a thing: Hvad er det? (What is that?). For a person, use hvem: Hvem er det? (Who is that?). Said alone, Hvad? means "Pardon?", but it can sound blunt, so Undskyld? (Excuse me?) is more polite.

sentence.da: **Hvad** hedder du?
sentence.en: What is your name?

hvad betyder det?.explanation: "Hvad betyder det?" means "What does that mean?". To ask about one word, put it after betyder (means): Hvad betyder 'hej'? (What does hej mean?).

sentence.da: Jeg forstår ikke ordet. **Hvad betyder det?**
sentence.en: I don't understand the word. What does that mean?

hvad er klokken?.explanation: "Hvad er klokken?" means "What time is it?" Literally, it asks what the clock is, because klokken means "the clock". You answer with klokken er (it is … o'clock) plus the time. A polite alternative is ved du, hvad klokken er? (do you know what time it is?).

sentence.da: Undskyld, **hvad er klokken?**
sentence.en: Excuse me, what time is it?

hvad hedder det på dansk?.explanation: "Hvad hedder det på dansk?" means "What is that called in Danish?". Hedder means "is called", the same word used for names: jeg hedder Anna (my name is Anna).

forms.en: What is that called in Danish?
What is that called in English?

sentence.da: Undskyld, **hvad hedder det på dansk?**
sentence.en: Excuse me, what is that called in Danish?

hvad hedder du?.explanation: "Hvad hedder du?" means "What's your name?" Literally, it asks what you are called. You answer Jeg hedder Anna (My name is Anna).

sentence.da: **Hvad hedder du?** - Jeg hedder Anna.
sentence.en: What's your name? - My name is Anna.

hvad koster det?.explanation: "Hvad koster det?" means "How much does it cost?". Say det for things like et hus (a house) and den for things like en bog (a book): hvad koster den? For several things, say hvad koster de? (how much are they?).

sentence.da: **Hvad koster det?** Jeg vil gerne købe det.
sentence.en: How much does it cost? I'd like to buy it.

hvad laver du?.explanation: "Hvad laver du?" means "What are you doing?" and can mean right now or in general (like What do you do?). To ask about someone's job, hvad arbejder du med? (what do you work with?) is clearer. With several people, say hvad laver I? (what are you all doing?).

forms.en: What are you doing at the weekend?

related.en: what are you going to do?

sentence.da: **Hvad laver du** i aften?
sentence.en: What are you doing tonight?

hvad med dig?.explanation: "Hvad med dig?" means "What about you?" and turns a question back to the other person. Use hvad med jer? (what about you all?) for several people. You can put anyone in place of dig, for example hvad med Anna? (what about Anna?).

sentence.da: Jeg har det godt. **Hvad med dig?**
sentence.en: I'm doing well. What about you?

hvad som helst.explanation: "Hvad som helst" means "anything", with no limit. For people, use hvem som helst (anyone).

forms.da: Du kan vælge hvad som helst.

sentence.da: Jeg er sulten og spiser **hvad som helst**.
sentence.en: I am hungry and will eat anything.

hvad så?.explanation: "Hvad så?" means "what's up?" (literally, what then?). It is a casual greeting you use with friends and people you know well, instead of hvordan har du det? (how are you?).

sentence.da: Hej Anna, **hvad så?**
sentence.en: Hi Anna, what's up?

hvede.explanation: "Hvede" means "wheat", the grain that white bread, pasta and most cakes are made from. Danes also use rug (rye) for dark bread: rugbrød (rye bread).

sentence.da: Af **hvede** laver man mel, og af mel bager man brød.
sentence.en: From wheat you make flour, and from flour you bake bread.

hvedemel.explanation: "Hvedemel" means "wheat flour", the usual flour for baking. It is built from hvede (wheat) and mel (flour), and hvede also appears in hvedebrød (wheat bread).

sentence.da: Jeg bager boller med **hvedemel** og vand.
sentence.en: I bake buns with wheat flour and water.

hvem.explanation: "Hvem" means "who" and asks about a person. Compare Hvad er det? (What is that? - a thing) with Hvem er det? (Who is that? - a person). It also works after small words like med (with): Med hvem skal du rejse? (Who are you traveling with?).

sentence.da: **Hvem** er din lærer?
sentence.en: Who is your teacher?

hvem som helst.explanation: "Hvem som helst" means "anyone" and is about people. For things, use hvad som helst (anything).

forms.da: Hvem som helst kan være med.

sentence.da: I dag kan **hvem som helst** lære at svømme.
sentence.en: Today anyone can learn to swim.

hver.explanation: "Hver" means "each" or "every". Compare hver dag (every day) with hvert år (every year): hver goes with en-words like dag, and hvert goes with et-words like år.

sentence.da: Jeg løber **hver** morgen.
sentence.en: I run every morning.

hver dag.explanation: "Hver dag" means "every day". Hver (each, every) goes with en-words like dag (day); with et-words it becomes hvert, as in hvert år (every year).

sentence.da: Jeg drikker kaffe **hver dag**.
sentence.en: I drink coffee every day.

hverken.explanation: "Hverken" means "neither" and works with eller (or) as a pair: hverken ... eller (neither ... nor).

forms.da: hverken i dag eller i morgen

sentence.da: Jeg vil **hverken** have kaffe eller te.
sentence.en: I want neither coffee nor tea.

hverken…eller.explanation: "Hverken…eller" means "neither…nor" and joins two things in a no: Jeg har hverken tid eller penge (I have neither time nor money). Do not add ikke (not), because hverken already makes it a no.

forms.da: hverken i dag eller i morgen

sentence.da: Kaffe eller te? **Hverken…eller**, tak. Jeg tager vand.
sentence.en: Coffee or tea? Neither, thanks. I will have water.

hvert.explanation: "Hvert" means "each" or "every" and goes before et-words. Before en-words, use hver instead: hver dag (every day), hver bil (each car).

sentence.da: Vi rejser **hvert** år til Sverige.
sentence.en: We travel to Sweden every year.

hvid.explanation: "Hvid" means "white". The h at the start is silent, so the word starts with a v sound.

sentence.da: Sneen er kold og **hvid**.
sentence.en: The snow is cold and white.

hvidløg.explanation: "Hvidløg" means "garlic". It is made of hvid (white) and løg (onion), so it is literally white onion. Garlic is counted in cloves: to fed hvidløg (two cloves of garlic).

sentence.da: **Hvidløg** er hvidt og lugter stærkt.
sentence.en: Garlic is white and smells strong.

hvilke.explanation: "Hvilke" means "which" when you ask about more than one thing. For one thing, use hvilken (en-words) or hvilket (et-words): hvilken bil (which car), hvilket hus (which house).

sentence.da: **Hvilke** sko vil du have?
sentence.en: Which shoes do you want?

hvilken.explanation: "Hvilken" means "which". Compare Hvad vil du have? (What do you want?) with Hvilken bil vil du have? (Which car do you want?): hvad stands alone, while hvilken comes right before the thing you are asking about.

sentence.da: **Hvilken** farve kan du bedst lide?
sentence.en: Which color do you like best?

hvilket.explanation: "Hvilket" means "which" and is used with et-words. With en-words, use hvilken: Hvilken bil? (Which car?).

sentence.da: **Hvilket** hus er dit?
sentence.en: Which house is yours?

hvis.explanation: "Hvis" means "if" and sets a condition. Do not mix it up with om (whether), as in Jeg ved ikke, om han kommer (I don't know whether he is coming).

sentence.da: Jeg bliver hjemme, **hvis** det regner.
sentence.en: I stay home if it rains.

hvis jeg var dig.explanation: "Hvis jeg var dig" means "if I were you" and opens a piece of advice: Hvis jeg var dig, ville jeg ringe til ham (If I were you, I would call him). Danish uses var (was) here, where English uses were.

sentence.da: **Hvis jeg var dig**, ville jeg blive hjemme.
sentence.en: If I were you, I would stay home.

hvor.explanation: "Hvor" means "where". Before a word that describes, it means "how": hvor gammel (how old), hvor meget (how much), hvor mange (how many).

sentence.da: **Hvor** er stationen?
sentence.en: Where is the station?

hvor er toilettet?.explanation: "Hvor er toilettet?" means "Where is the restroom?" It is made of hvor (where), er (is) and toilettet (the toilet). Starting with undskyld (excuse me) makes it polite.

sentence.da: Undskyld, **hvor er toilettet?**
sentence.en: Excuse me, where is the restroom?

hvor gammel er du?.explanation: "Hvor gammel er du?" means "How old are you?" It is made of hvor (how), gammel (old), er (is) and du (you). In the answer, you can leave out gammel: Jeg er tyve år (I am twenty years old).

sentence.da: Anna, **hvor gammel er du?**
sentence.en: Anna, how old are you?

hvor kommer du fra?.explanation: "Hvor kommer du fra?" means "Where are you from?" Literally, it is Where do you come from? You answer Jeg kommer fra England (I come from England). As in English, fra (from) goes at the end of the question.

forms.en: Where do you all come from?

sentence.da: Hej, **hvor kommer du fra?**
sentence.en: Hi, where are you from?

hvor meget koster det?.explanation: "Hvor meget koster det?" means "How much does it cost?" Word by word, it is how much costs it. Hvor meget (how much) works with other verbs too: Hvor meget vejer det? (How much does it weigh?)

forms.en: How much does it cost? (for an en-word thing)

sentence.da: Jeg vil købe brødet. **Hvor meget koster det?**
sentence.en: I want to buy the bread. How much does it cost?

hvor som helst.explanation: "Hvor som helst" means "anywhere", with no limit on the place. Som helst (no matter which) can follow other question words too: hvem som helst (anyone), hvad som helst (anything), hvornår som helst (any time).

forms.da: Du kan bo hvor som helst.

sentence.da: Du kan sidde **hvor som helst** i rummet.
sentence.en: You can sit anywhere in the room.

hvordan.explanation: "Hvordan" means "how" and asks in what way something is done. Before a word like old, much or many, Danish uses hvor instead: Hvor gammel er du? (How old are you?), Hvor mange børn har du? (How many children do you have?).

sentence.da: **Hvordan** kommer jeg til stationen?
sentence.en: How do I get to the station?

hvordan går det?.explanation: "Hvordan går det?" means "How's it going?" A normal answer is Det går godt, tak (It's going well, thanks), and you can ask back with og dig? (and you?).

sentence.da: Hej Anna, **hvordan går det?**
sentence.en: Hi Anna, how's it going?

hvordan har du det?.explanation: "Hvordan har du det?" means "How are you?" Literally, it is how have you it. Answer with Jeg har det godt (I'm doing well) or Fint, tak (Fine, thanks).

sentence.da: Hej Peter! **Hvordan har du det?**
sentence.en: Hi Peter! How are you?

hvorefter.explanation: "Hvorefter" means "after which", joining two events so that the second follows right after the first. It is built from hvor (which) and efter (after). In casual talk, Danes often say og så (and then) instead.

forms.en: after which it began to rain

sentence.da: Hun lukkede bogen, **hvorefter** hun slukkede lyset og sov.
sentence.en: She closed the book, after which she turned off the light and slept.

hvorfor.explanation: "Hvorfor" means "why" and asks for a reason. The answer often starts with fordi (because): Hvorfor kommer du ikke? - Fordi jeg er syg. (Why aren't you coming? - Because I am sick.)

sentence.da: **Hvorfor** er du så glad?
sentence.en: Why are you so happy?

hvorfra.explanation: "Hvorfra" means "from where" and asks about a starting point. To ask where someone is going, use hvorhen (where to): Hvorhen skal du? (Where are you going?).

forms.en: Where does the bus come from?

sentence.da: **Hvorfra** kommer din ven?
sentence.en: Where does your friend come from?

hvorimod.explanation: "Hvorimod" means "whereas", setting one fact against another that is different. It is not used for time. For "at the same time", use mens (while): Jeg læser, mens du sover (I read while you sleep).

sentence.da: Jeg bor i byen, **hvorimod** min søster bor på landet.
sentence.en: I live in the city, whereas my sister lives in the country.

hvornår.explanation: "Hvornår" means "when" in a question. In the middle of a sentence, use når for when: Jeg ringer, når jeg kommer hjem (I will call when I get home). For one finished event in the past, use da: Jeg var glad, da du kom (I was happy when you came).

sentence.da: **Hvornår** åbner butikken?
sentence.en: When does the shop open?

hvorved.explanation: "Hvorved" means "whereby" or "by which", linking a result to the way it came about: Han trykkede på knappen, hvorved døren åbnede sig (He pressed the button, by which the door opened). It is mostly found in writing.

sentence.da: Hun skrev under, **hvorved** aftalen blev gyldig.
sentence.en: She signed, whereby the agreement became valid.

hvorvidt.explanation: "Hvorvidt" means "whether". It does the same job as om (if) in a sentence like Jeg ved ikke, om han kommer (I do not know if he is coming), but it sounds more like writing than speech.

forms.da: Jeg ved ikke, hvorvidt han kommer
forms.en: I do not know whether he is coming

forms.da: spørgsmålet er hvorvidt det er muligt
forms.en: the question is whether it is possible

sentence.da: Politiet undersøger, **hvorvidt** manden har sagt sandheden.
sentence.en: The police are investigating whether the man has told the truth.

hygge.explanation: "Hygge" means "coziness", the warm, relaxed feeling of being together with candles, food and good company.

forms.en: We have a cozy time at home

sentence.da: Vi tænder lys og har **hygge** hjemme.
sentence.en: We light candles and have a cozy time at home.

hyggelig.explanation: "Hyggelig" means "cozy", "pleasant" or "nice". It describes a place, an evening or a person: Han er hyggelig means "He is nice to be around". It comes from hygge (a warm, relaxed, cozy feeling).

sentence.da: Det var en **hyggelig** aften.
sentence.en: It was a cozy evening.

hyggeligt at møde dig.explanation: "Hyggeligt at møde dig" means nice to meet you (literally cozy to meet you). Reply with I lige måde (likewise). For someone you already know, say hyggeligt at se dig (nice to see you).

sentence.da: Jeg hedder Maja. **Hyggeligt at møde dig.**
sentence.en: I'm Maja. Nice to meet you.

hyppig.explanation: "Hyppig" means "frequent", happening many times. It also works for how something is done: Han besøger os hyppigt (He visits us frequently).

sentence.da: Forkølelse er en **hyppig** sygdom om vinteren.
sentence.en: A cold is a frequent illness in the winter.

hysterisk.explanation: "Hysterisk" means "hysterical", showing feelings so strong that a person loses control, like fear or laughter. In everyday speech, it can also just mean very funny: hysterisk sjov (hilariously funny).

sentence.da: Hun blev **hysterisk** af skræk og begyndte at skrige.
sentence.en: She became hysterical from fright and began to scream.

hytteost.explanation: "Hytteost" means "cottage cheese", a soft, fresh cheese. It is hytte (cottage) and ost (cheese) joined together, and it is often eaten with fruit.

sentence.da: **Hytteost** er en hvid ost med små klumper.
sentence.en: Cottage cheese is a white cheese with small lumps.

håb.explanation: "Håb" means "hope", the thing you hope for. To say you hope, use håber: Jeg håber, det virker (I hope it works).

sentence.da: Der er stadig **håb** for holdet.
sentence.en: There is still hope for the team.

håbefuld.explanation: "Håbefuld" means "hopeful", full of hope that things will go well. It is built from håb (hope) and the ending -fuld (full of), which is also in smertefuld (painful).

sentence.da: Hun er **håbefuld** og tror på en lykkelig slutning.
sentence.en: She is hopeful and believes in a happy ending.

håbløs.explanation: "Håbløs" means "hopeless", with no hope that things will get better. In everyday talk, it can also describe a person who is very bad at something: Jeg er håbløs til matematik (I am hopeless at math).

sentence.da: Situationen virker **håbløs**, og alle har givet op.
sentence.en: The situation seems hopeless, and everyone has given up.

håndbagage.explanation: "Håndbagage" means "carry-on luggage", what you take with you into the plane cabin. The luggage you hand in at check-in is indchecket bagage (checked luggage).

sentence.da: Jeg har kun **håndbagage** i flyet.
sentence.en: I only have carry-on luggage on the plane.

håndbold.explanation: "Håndbold" means "handball", the team sport. It is made of hånd (hand) and bold (ball). For the sport, you leave out en: Jeg spiller håndbold (I play handball). En håndbold is the ball itself.

sentence.da: **Håndbold** spilles med hænderne og en bold.
sentence.en: Handball is played with the hands and a ball.

hår.explanation: "Hår" means "hair", all the hair on your head or body. One single strand is et hår (a hair).

sentence.da: Hun har langt **hår**.
sentence.en: She has long hair.

hård.explanation: "Hård" means "hard" as in firm, not soft. It can also mean tough: et hårdt job (a tough job). For "hard" meaning "difficult", Danes usually say svær (difficult): en svær opgave (a difficult task).

sentence.da: Stenen er **hård** og kold.
sentence.en: The stone is hard and cold.

hårdhudet.explanation: "Hårdhudet" means "thick-skinned", not easily hurt by criticism or harsh words. It can also describe real skin that has become hard and rough: hårdhudede hænder (hands with rough skin).

sentence.da: Kritik går ikke ind på ham, fordi han er **hårdhudet**.
sentence.en: Criticism does not get to him because he is thick-skinned.

hævet.explanation: "Hævet" means "swollen", puffed up from an injury or an infection. The same word is used for dough that has risen: hævet dej (risen dough).

sentence.da: Jeg faldt på trappen, og nu er min fod **hævet**.
sentence.en: I fell on the stairs, and now my foot is swollen.

hævn.explanation: "En hævn" means "revenge", doing harm to someone because they harmed you. It is mostly used without en, as in at tage hævn (to take revenge), and the verb is at hævne (to avenge).

sentence.da: Han søgte **hævn**, fordi de havde ødelagt hans firma.
sentence.en: He sought revenge because they had ruined his company.

hø.explanation: "Hø" means "hay", grass that is cut and dried to feed animals in winter. Do not mix it up with halm (straw), which is the dry stalks left after grain is harvested.

sentence.da: Om vinteren får køerne **hø**, fordi der ikke er frisk græs.
sentence.en: In winter, the cows get hay because there is no fresh grass.

høfeber.explanation: "Høfeber" means "hay fever", a reaction to pollen from grass and trees that gives a runny nose and itchy eyes. It is built the same way as in English, from hø (hay) and feber (fever), though you have no fever.

sentence.da: Om foråret har jeg **høfeber** og klør i øjnene.
sentence.en: In spring, I have hay fever and itchy eyes.

høflig.explanation: "Høflig" means "polite", for people and how they behave. Saying tak (thanks) and undskyld (sorry) is polite.

sentence.da: Han er altid **høflig** og siger tak.
sentence.en: He is always polite and says thanks.

høflighed.explanation: "Høflighed" means "politeness", being kind and respectful to others. It is built from høflig (polite), and -hed turns a describing word into the quality itself: fri (free) becomes frihed (freedom).

sentence.da: Han sagde tak af **høflighed**.
sentence.en: He said thanks out of politeness.

høj.explanation: "Høj" means "tall" or "high", for people and for things. Højt also means "loudly": Tal højt means "Speak loudly".

sentence.da: Giraffen er meget **høj**.
sentence.en: The giraffe is very tall.

højlydt.explanation: "Højlydt" means "loud" for noisy people or noisy actions: Hun lo højlydt (She laughed loudly). It is built from høj (high) and lyd (sound).

sentence.da: Det var en **højlydt** fest.
sentence.en: It was a loud party.

højre.explanation: "Højre" means "right", as in the right side or the right hand. For directions, you say til højre (to the right): Drej til højre (Turn right).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver med min **højre** hånd.
sentence.en: I write with my right hand.

højst.explanation: "Højst" means "at most", the upper limit: Du må højst tage to (You may take two at most). Before a describing word it means "highly": højst usandsynligt (highly unlikely).

sentence.da: Hun er **højst** tyve år gammel.
sentence.en: She is at most twenty years old.

højtidelig.explanation: "Højtidelig" means "solemn", for a moment or event that feels dignified and important, such as a wedding or a funeral. It can also describe a person's tone: hun talte højtideligt (she spoke in a solemn way).

sentence.da: Ceremonien var **højtidelig**, og alle var klædt fint på.
sentence.en: The ceremony was solemn and everyone was dressed up.

hørelse.explanation: "En hørelse" means "hearing", the sense that lets you pick up sounds. It is about the ability, not about listening to something: for that, use at lytte (to listen).

sentence.da: Efter mange år på fabrikken er hans **hørelse** blevet dårlig.
sentence.en: After many years at the factory, his hearing has become bad.

høretelefoner.explanation: "Høretelefoner" means "headphones". The word is built from at høre (to hear) and telefon (phone). You wear them to listen without bothering others: Jeg bruger høretelefoner i toget (I use headphones on the train).

sentence.da: Jeg lytter til musik i mine **høretelefoner**.
sentence.en: I listen to music in my headphones.
